note: complete per-asset verdicts from the gold pass. band is post-verification. Fix against verifyWhy, never defect: 31% of defect lines were wrong about the cause while the verdict stood.

rows.readsAs: an elephant
rows.defect: the ear is a hard-edged oval with vertical ribs pasted on the shoulder well behind the eye — it reads as a slotted grille/radiator plate, not a fan-shaped ear, and its outline does not merge with the head
rows.fix: attach the ear at the skull behind the eye and paint it as a soft-edged fan lobe in a slightly darker hide tone with a few radial creases; delete the regular vertical rib hatching

rows.readsAs: a pale cow with two upright antlers
rows.defect: both horns spring from the top of the skull above and behind the eye, exactly the error the reference row calls out ('horn rising from the nose, not the forehead'); hide is smooth speckled grey with no plates or folds
rows.fix: anchor horn #1 on the nasal tip at the front of the muzzle and horn #2 just behind it; add 3-4 deep dark hide folds at the shoulder and haunch so the plated skin reads
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at 300px (goldpass/s1.png). Two cream cones rise from the CROWN, both bases sitting above and behind the large eye; the nose at the far right of the muzzle is bare. That is verbatim the error fauna.json's row anticipates ('horn rising from the nose, not the forehead'). mustRead 2 also fails: hide is a smooth pale grey with a fine crackle texture, zero plates or folds. mustRead 3 partly holds (barrel body, stumpy legs). Eyes are large with a specular highlight where the row asks for 'small'. Nasal horn is the one trait that names the animal and it is not there — FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a brown cow wearing a cream donut
rows.defect: the horns are drawn as one closed cream torus looping in front of the muzzle — an impossible shape that reads as a pasted ring; no white stockings on the legs and no shoulder ridge (topline is flat)
rows.fix: replace the ring with two separate horns sweeping out then up, tips open and not meeting; paint the lower third of all four legs white; raise the dorsal line over the withers into a muscular ridge
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, on the artifact ground rather than all three of the auditor's. The horns are one CLOSED cream annulus — both ends meet, forming a torus that floats in front of the muzzle. That is impossible geometry and reads as a pasted ring at any size; it is a visible drawing artifact on its own. Partial refutation of the auditor: the legs ARE noticeably paler than the brown body, so 'white stockings' is half-met, and there is a faint shoulder rise. Doesn't matter — the ring carries the FAIL, and the same ring is reused on Banteng, Water Buffalo and Buffalo.

rows.readsAs: an orange cow with the same cream donut horns
rows.defect: every one of its three mustReads is missing — no white rump patch, no white lower legs, no white muzzle band — and it is the Gaur asset recoloured orange with the same closed-loop horn ring
rows.fix: add a hard-edged white rump patch, white socks below the hock/knee and a white band across the bridge of the nose; open the horn ring into two crescents and add the bald pale forehead plate between them
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. Same closed cream torus as Gaur, and the tile is the Gaur asset recoloured orange — same silhouette, same tail tassel, same head. Of the row's three mustReads: no white rump patch (rump is orange), no white band above the muzzle, and the legs are a uniform pale tan over their whole length rather than white LOWER legs, so at best a third of one is met. No bald forehead plate between the horns either. Different-organism test: reads as an orange cow wearing a ring.

rows.readsAs: the Gaur again, in grey
rows.defect: the horns curl forward into a closed cream ring around the face instead of sweeping back over the shoulders, and the silhouette is pixel-identical to Gaur and Buffalo apart from coat colour
rows.fix: draw the horns as two long low crescents starting wide at the poll and sweeping BACK past the ear toward the shoulder; drop the topline flat and lengthen the barrel so it sits lower than the Gaur's
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, and the duplication is worse than reported. mustRead 1 asks for enormous SWEPT-BACK crescents; what is drawn is the same forward-closing cream ring used on Gaur/Banteng/Buffalo — the horns point the wrong direction and close on themselves. Side-by-side render (goldpass/b2.png) shows Water Buffalo and Buffalo as effectively the same picture, same grey, same ring, so they are not even separable by coat colour as the auditor assumed. mustRead 2 (heavy low-slung straight back) is roughly met; mustRead 3 (broad flat wet muzzle held low) is not — the head is carried high on a small muzzle.

rows.readsAs: a spotted deer
a tan antelope
a shaggy grey sheep or musk ox
rows.defect: the head is a featureless dark ball with a short blunt muzzle, there is no pale chest blaze at all, and the coat is mid-grey rather than black — nothing on the tile says 'bear'
rows.fix: darken the coat to near-black, extend the muzzle into a long pale grey mobile snout projecting past the brow, paint a cream U-shaped blaze across the chest, and add long curved claws at the forefeet
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. At 300px it is a shaggy pale-grey barrel on four thin columns with a dark ball head; the shape at the top of the head reads as a curled ram horn, not an ear. All three mustReads fail: coat is mid/pale grey not black and there is no shoulder mane, there is no pale U/Y chest blaze anywhere, and the snout is a short blunt stub with no long pale mobile muzzle and no claws at all (feet are small dark hoof-like blobs). Shares its entire body with Spectacled Bear and Mountain Tapir. A stranger names a sheep or musk ox.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey monkey
rows.defect: the face is the same grey as the coat so the bare pink face never reads, and the tail is a long body-length curl instead of the macaque's short-to-medium tail
rows.fix: paint the facial mask in a pink/red flesh tone distinct from the coat, and shorten the tail to roughly half the body length

rows.readsAs: the Macaque again, paler
rows.defect: the black face and black hands that separate a langur from a macaque are absent — face and hands are painted at coat tone — and there is no crown crest
rows.fix: paint the face disc and both hands/feet near-black against the pale silver coat, and add a short upright crest tuft on the crown

rows.readsAs: a small pale ferret
rows.defect: the tail is a short bushy stub; the reference calls for a thick tail tapering to a point nearly as long as the body, and the cream-white coat misses the grizzled grey
rows.fix: lengthen the tail to ~0.8 body length with a smooth taper to a point, and grizzle the coat with fine dark banding over grey

rows.readsAs: a tan dog with pony legs
rows.defect: the tail is uniform tan with no dark tip, and the legs are straight untapered columns with no visible hock or elbow so the body reads equine rather than canid
rows.fix: paint the distal third of the tail near-black and bush it out; put an angled hock in the hind leg and taper the limbs toward the paw

rows.readsAs: a hedgehog
rows.defect: the quills radiate as a starburst up and forward over the head, several crossing in front of the face, instead of lying back over the rump, and they are plain white with no bands
rows.fix: rake all quills backward at 20-40 degrees from the shoulder to the rump, longest over the hips, none forward of the ear; alternate black and cream bands along each quill

rows.readsAs: a rabbit with a squirrel tail
rows.defect: the ears are tall pink-lined uprights that read unmistakably as a rabbit's; the squirrel's ears are small and rounded, and the eye is too small for the 'prominent' spec
rows.fix: halve the ear height and round the tips, drop the pink inner lining, and enlarge the eye to a big dark dome

rows.readsAs: a teal bird with a short spoked fan
rows.defect: the train is only about one body length and is drawn as a flat rigid spoke fan with dots on the spoke tips; the reference calls for an extremely long trailing train, and the plumage is cyan-teal rather than deep iridescent blue
rows.fix: extend the train to 2-3x body length trailing behind and below the bird, soften the spokes into drooping barbs, and place the blue-gold ocelli along the length rather than only at the tips; deepen the neck/breast to royal blue

rows.readsAs: a worm with an armoured helmet on its head
rows.defect: the hood is a bulbous ribbed ovoid larger than the body, pasted over the head with a disc eye stuck onto it, and the snake lies flat — the front third is not reared at all
rows.fix: rear the front third vertically off the coil and paint the hood as a flat spread of skin BEHIND the head, wider than the head and thinner than it, with the head silhouette still visible in front of it
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, with the auditor's wording sharpened. A hood-shaped mass IS present, so 'no hood' overstates — but it is drawn as a frontal ovoid shield with radiating ribs and a scalloped fan skirt, pasted onto a side-view body, with the slit eye sitting on the shield rather than on a head. The perspective mismatch is what makes it read as armour. Decisive failure is mustRead 2: the front third is not reared at all, the whole animal lies flat, and the row's note is explicit ('the reared cobra is taller than it is wide', aspect 1.1) while the render is roughly 2:1 wide. Body ribbing reads as annelid segments and is shared with Viper.

rows.readsAs: a newt or salamander
rows.defect: the limbs are tiny stubs barely clearing the body outline, there is no forked tongue, and the neck is short — a monitor's defining sprawled muscular legs with hooked claws are absent
rows.fix: lengthen the limbs to sprawl clear of the body with a bent elbow/knee and splayed clawed toes, add a long forked tongue flicking from the snout, and stretch the neck to about a third of the trunk
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, and stronger than reported. In the 300px render (goldpass/s6.png) I can find NO limbs at all — the belly line is unbroken; the 'tiny stubs' the auditor saw on the 42-sheet are not resolvable as legs. mustRead 3 (muscular sprawled limbs with large hooked claws) is therefore wholly absent. No forked tongue (mustRead 1 absent). The tail is long but a smooth round taper, not laterally flattened. The row's note calls for a long snake-like neck; head merges straight into body. Reads as a newt or a fish.

rows.readsAs: a turtle
rows.defect: the four legs are identical featureless rectangular posts with no feet — no webbing, no claws, no taper — so the animal reads as a shell on table legs
rows.fix: replace the posts with short splayed limbs ending in a webbed flipper-foot with 3-4 visible claws; angle the forelimbs forward and hindlimbs back

rows.readsAs: a cartoon frog
rows.defect: the large circular tympanum behind the eye — the row's first mustRead and the trait that names this frog — is absent, and the hind legs are thin stubs rather than powerful folded jumpers
rows.fix: add a flat circular eardrum disc just behind and below each eye, drawn slightly larger than the eye in a paler green; thicken the hind limb into a folded Z with a bulging thigh and a webbed foot

rows.readsAs: a pale ant
rows.defect: the body is three separated spheres joined by pinched waists, which is exactly the wasp-waisted ant profile the reference row warns against
rows.fix: merge thorax and abdomen with a broad joint at least 70% of the abdomen's width so the outline is continuous, and swell the abdomen into a soft translucent teardrop

rows.readsAs: a housefly
rows.defect: the wings are spread flat out sideways behind a small grey body and the two eyes are big spheres bulging forward off the front of the head — the tented roof wing posture and the blunt wide head with corner-set eyes are both absent
rows.fix: fold the wings into a steep tent along the midline so they overlap over the abdomen and reach past its tip, widen the head into a blunt flat plate with the eyes set at its two outer corners, and add visible wing venation
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. Wings are spread flat out sideways — the row's note says in so many words 'wings are held tent-like over the back at rest, not spread flat', so mustRead 1 is failed against an explicit instruction. mustRead 2 also fails: the eyes are two grey spheres bulging FORWARD off the front of a small head instead of being pushed to the corners of a blunt wide head. Only mustRead 3 (short stout body) survives. Flat wings plus forward eye-spheres is the housefly read; confirmed.

rows.readsAs: a grasshopper
rows.defect: there are no raptorial forelegs folded in prayer and no long slender prothorax — the body is a plain green ellipse with thin walking legs and flat spread wings, so it reads as an orthopteran
rows.fix: add a long narrow prothorax raising the front of the body, and mount two thick forelegs on it folded in a Z with a spined inner edge held up under the triangular head; drop the wings flat along the back instead of spread
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, with one correction: a thin bent Z-shaped foreleg IS drawn at the front, so 'no raptorial forelegs' overstates — but it is a bare line with no spines and no thickness, and it does not read as an arm folded in prayer. The other two mustReads are simply absent: the head is a round blob with no neck (the row's note: 'only a mantis truly has a neck'), and there is no long slender prothorax — the head sits straight on a fat ellipse. Posture is specified 'upright' at aspect 1.0; the render is horizontal at roughly 2:1. Thin walking legs plus flat spread wings = grasshopper.

rows.readsAs: a male lion
a giraffe
a zebra with painted-on stripes
rows.defect: the stripes stop at a hard rectangular edge on the barrel — the legs, belly and rump are plain white, contradicting 'stripes continuing onto the legs and belly'
rows.fix: carry the stripe field over the rump, down all four legs to the hoof, and across the belly, letting the bands narrow and bend as they wrap; remove the straight vertical cutoff at the flank

rows.readsAs: a striped antelope
rows.defect: the flank stripes are painted as dark brown scratches on tan when a kudu's are thin WHITE bars, and the ears are small pointed nubs rather than the huge rounded satellite dishes the row names
rows.fix: switch the flank bars to near-white at ~60% opacity, 6-10 of them evenly spaced and vertical; scale the ears to roughly head-height, rounded not pointed, and splay them outward

rows.readsAs: a golden antelope
rows.defect: the black rump striping and the black tuft above the hind hoof are both missing, and the horns hook forward at the tips instead of the lyre sweep out-then-up
rows.fix: add a white rump patch bounded by two vertical black stripes plus a black tail stripe, a black tuft on the rear cannon bone, and re-curve the horns outward then upward with the tips diverging

rows.readsAs: a shaggy pig
rows.defect: the erect bristly mane along the neck and spine is absent (the topline is bare) and the tail hangs down with a tuft instead of standing straight up; the flank is covered in long hair a warthog does not have
rows.fix: add a stiff upright bristle crest from the poll along the spine to mid-back, rotate the tail to vertical with the tuft at the top, and thin the body hair to sparse bristles over bare hide

rows.readsAs: the Gaur asset in grey
rows.defect: the horns are the same closed cream ring used on Gaur/Banteng/Water Buffalo — there is no fused boss across the forehead — and the big fringed drooping ears are absent
rows.fix: join the horn bases into a solid helmet boss covering the forehead, then drop each horn down and out before hooking up; hang large fringed ears BELOW the horns on each side
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. mustRead 1 asks for horns FUSED into a solid boss across the forehead; the tile has the same detached closed cream ring as Gaur/Banteng/Water Buffalo — no boss, and an impossible shape. mustRead 3 (large fringed drooping ears hanging below the horns) is absent: the ears are two small dark triangles above the ring. mustRead 2 (massive shoulders, thick neck) is not met either, the topline is flat. Rendered next to Water Buffalo the two are the same picture.

rows.readsAs: a spotted dog
rows.defect: the topline is level — the forelegs and hind legs are the same length, so the skeletal shoulder-to-hip slope that defines a spotted hyena never appears; the spots are large ragged brown blotches rather than small round dark spots
rows.fix: lengthen the forelegs ~15% over the hind legs and drop the croup so the back slopes visibly down to the rear; shrink the spots to small discrete rounds scattered over flank and haunch

rows.readsAs: a brown monkey
rows.defect: the face is flat with a tiny muzzle — the long dog-like snout with close-set eyes that names a baboon is absent — and there is no shoulder cape
rows.fix: project the muzzle forward to roughly a third of head length with the nostrils at its tip and the eyes set close together high on the brow; add a mantle of long hair over the shoulders

rows.readsAs: a lamb
rows.defect: the animal stands on all fours as a pale quadruped — the sentinel upright posture propped on hind legs and tail, the dark eye rings and the black tail tip are all absent, and the aspect is landscape where the row specifies 0.5 (taller than wide)
rows.fix: switch this species to the upright posture: rear on the hind legs with the tail as a third prop, forepaws held at the chest; add dark rings around both eyes and blacken the last quarter of the thin tapering tail
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed on all counts, and it is the clearest failure in the set. The row specifies posture 'upright' and aspect 0.5 (much taller than wide); the render is a landscape quadruped standing squarely on four legs. All three mustReads absent: no sentinel stance propped on hind legs and tail, no dark eye rings, no black tail tip (the tail is a short uniform pale curl). Reads as a lamb or kid goat.

rows.readsAs: a ginger housecat
rows.defect: the long black ear tufts — the single trait that names a caracal — are absent, the ear is a plain small triangle, and the tail is long and curled up over the back instead of short
rows.fix: add a black tuft of 4-6 stiff hairs trailing from each ear tip, about half the ear's height again; blacken the back of the ear; cut the tail to about a third of body length and drop it
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. mustRead 1 — the long black tufts trailing from the ear tips, the single trait the animal is named for — is absent; the ears are small dark triangles with no trailing hair. mustRead 3 fails in both halves: the tail is long and curls up over the back where the row demands a short tail. Only mustRead 2 (plain reddish-tan coat) is met. The feet also read as small pale hooves rather than paws, pushing it further from a cat. A stranger names a ginger dog or fawn.

rows.readsAs: a vulture
rows.defect: the neck ruff is a hard-edged solid white ellipse pasted on the breast — it has no feather texture and its outline cuts across the body silhouette like a sticker
rows.fix: redraw the ruff as a soft collar of short pale feathers wrapping the base of the bare neck, with a broken feathery lower edge rather than a clean ellipse, and hunch the shoulders above it

rows.readsAs: a grey pigeon
rows.defect: the dense white pearl spotting that defines a guineafowl is entirely absent — the body is plain slate grey with a few concentric arcs — and the head carries a spiky punk crest instead of a bare bony casque
rows.fix: stipple the whole body, wings and neck with small evenly spaced white dots; replace the crest with a smooth horn-coloured casque rising off the crown and paint the bare head blue with red facial wattles
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. mustRead 2's defining half — the dense white pearl spotting — is entirely absent; the body is plain slate grey with a few concentric arcs, and that spotting is the trait the bird is known by. mustRead 1 fails too: instead of a tiny bare blue-and-red head with a bony helmet casque there is a feathered spiky crest on a normally-coloured head. The hunched round body, thin neck and yellow legs (mustRead 3) are the only things that hold, and unspotted they read pigeon or grey quail.

rows.readsAs: an earthworm with a tongue
rows.defect: the head is a smooth rounded oval no wider than the neck, there is no zigzag or diamond dorsal chain, and the body is long and thin rather than short and heavy — the ringed body shading reads as annelid segments
rows.fix: widen the head into a broad triangle clearly stepped off a narrow neck, add a vertical-slit pupil, thicken the body to roughly 2x the neck width over a short length, and run a dark zigzag chain down the spine
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed — three of three mustReads absent. The head is a smooth rounded oval no wider than the neck, so there is no broad triangular head set off from a thin neck; there is no zigzag or diamond dorsal chain, the dorsum is plain; and the body is a long thin uniform tube rather than short, thick and heavy. It is also the same coil asset as Cobra minus the hood, and the dense transverse ribbing reads as earthworm annulation. Nothing on the tile says viper.

rows.readsAs: a woven basket on table legs
rows.defect: the shell is a low wireframe dome of thin radial and concentric lines with no scute plates, and all four legs are identical featureless rectangular posts — the head is a smooth ball with a pasted white eye and no beak
rows.fix: raise the shell into a tall dome and fill it with discrete raised scutes each carrying concentric growth rings; replace the posts with columnar elephantine legs covered in coarse scales and blunt clubbed feet; add a hooked horny beak and a wrinkled neck
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, though it is the weakest FAIL here and the auditor's shell complaint is partly refutable — the radial-plus-concentric line work over a filled tan dome is a fair schematic of scute division, not a hollow wireframe. What holds it at FAIL is a visible drawing artifact plus a missing trait: the legs are literal hard-edged rectangles, untapered, with flat square bottoms and no feet or toes, and the head is a smooth ball with a pasted eye dot and no beak (mustRead 3 absent). The dome is also low and wide where mustRead 1 calls for a tall dome. Silhouette does read 'tortoise', so this fails on craft rather than identity.

rows.readsAs: a grasshopper
rows.defect: the hind jumping leg is drawn at the same hairline weight as the walking legs, so the hugely enlarged femur the row names does not read
rows.fix: thicken the hind femur into a broad spindle roughly a third of the body length and fold it into a sharp Z above the body line, keeping the tibia thin and spined

rows.readsAs: a beetle
rows.defect: the legs are thin wispy curves with no structure and the head is a small nub with two dots — the flat spade-shaped head and the toothed rake-like digging forelegs are both absent
rows.fix: widen the head into a flat semicircular spade projecting past the pronotum, and thicken the forelegs with 3-4 large teeth along the outer edge of each tibia

rows.readsAs: a scorpion, mostly by its tail
rows.defect: the pincers do not read — the pedipalps end in small solid blobs with no open chela — and the prosoma/abdomen is a chain of separate spheres rather than a flat broad body
rows.fix: end each pedipalp in a two-piece claw with a visible gap between the fixed and movable finger, held forward ahead of the head; flatten the body into one continuous broad segmented plate

rows.readsAs: a shaggy grey sheep
rows.defect: the silhouette is a hairy barrel on four short columns with no bear bulk, and the coat is pale grey-brown rather than blackish; the pale eye ring is there but has nothing bear-shaped to sit on
rows.fix: darken the coat to blackish, raise the shoulder mass and shorten the neck so the head sits low and forward, broaden the paws into plantigrade feet with visible claws, and widen the cream eye rings into full spectacles running down the muzzle
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, crediting what the auditor also credited: the pale eye ring IS clearly drawn (mustRead 1 met). The other two fail — the coat is pale grey-cream, not blackish, and it hangs in long fleece strands over a barrel with thin straight legs and small dark hoof-like feet, which is a sheep or highland goat build with no bear bulk and no plantigrade paws. The dark curl at the top of the head reads as a ram horn. Same body asset as Sloth Bear and Mountain Tapir. Stranger test: names a shaggy sheep.

rows.readsAs: a woolly grey pig
rows.defect: the short prehensile proboscis is absent — the muzzle is a plain blunt grey snout — and the white-rimmed lips are missing, so nothing distinguishes it from the Sloth Bear/Spectacled Bear asset it shares
rows.fix: extend the upper lip into a short flexible trunk drooping past the lower jaw, outline the lip margin in white, and arch the back into a high rounded croup falling away to the rump
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands but the auditor's reasoning is wrong in two places and I want that on record. The muzzle is NOT 'a plain blunt grey snout' — it is a distinctly enlarged mass that overhangs the lower jaw and droops, which is a defensible short proboscis, and the head is NOT the Sloth Bear/Spectacled Bear head (bigger muzzle, different ear). What actually fails: mustRead 3's white-rimmed lips are absent (one small pale fleck near the mouth is all there is), mustRead 2 is half-met at best (woolly yes, black no — it is mid-grey), and the body is the same fleece-strand barrel on thin legs shared with the two bears, which reads as a sheep rather than a stocky arch-backed tapir. Identity fails on the body, not the nose.

rows.readsAs: a pink ragworm with red bristle fringes
rows.defect: the head is a plain blunt pink knob with a single dark dot — none of the short tentacles or palps the reference names, so the front end is indistinguishable from the tail end
rows.fix: add 4-6 short tapering appendages fanning forward off the head segment (2 palps + 2-4 antennae), drawn a shade darker than the body so they separate from the pink

rows.readsAs: a generic tan marten or stoat
rows.defect: none of the three rodent cues are present: the tail is a short thin downward curl instead of a long naked rope, there are no orange incisors (the muzzle has no teeth at all), and the head is a small pointed carnivore snout rather than a blunt rounded rodent head
rows.fix: set tail length to ~0.9x body with constant thickness and a scaly cross-hatch texture, held low and straight behind; widen headFrac's skull to a blunt dome and paint two orange incisor rectangles at the mouth line
rows.verifyWhy: Stands up at size. fauna.json mustRead is [blunt rounded head with large orange incisors, long scaly rope-like tail, partly webbed hind feet] and all three are absent: the tail is a short thin tapered upward curl (~15% of body length, furred, not a naked rope), the muzzle is an elongate pointed carnivore snout with a dark nose and a closed mouth line carrying no incisors at all, and the feet are small dark rounded tips that read as hooves rather than webbed hind feet. Nothing on the tile is rodent-specific; a stranger names a marten, stoat or small dog. FAIL on 'defining trait absent' three times over.

rows.readsAs: a plump brown shorebird with a long straight bill
rows.defect: legs are drawn short and yellow-orange; the reference calls for long dark legs, and the cinnamon breast has no dark chevron barring — the body is one flat brown wash with a single dark wing oval
rows.fix: lengthen the tarsus to ~0.45x body height and recolour legs to near-black; add a row of dark V-chevrons across the breast/flank band

rows.readsAs: a white gull or egret
rows.defect: the bill is a straight yellow dagger — the avocet's defining strongly upswept needle bill is absent, so this tile is indistinguishable from the Gannet tile in the same slice; legs are yellow rather than blue-grey and there is no crisp black-and-white pied pattern
rows.fix: curve the bill upward through ~35 degrees along its length, thin it to a needle and colour it black; recolour legs blue-grey; add black crown/nape and black wing-coverts blocks against the white body
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed at size. The bill is a straight yellow dagger angled very slightly DOWN — the reference note is explicit that 'the bill curves up, not down', and the upswept needle bill is the one cue that separates an avocet from every other white wader. Legs are yellow, not the required long blue-grey; the plumage is white with a mid-grey wing panel and a grey tail wedge, not crisp black-and-white pied. All three mustRead items fail. A stranger names a gull, egret or generic tern.

rows.readsAs: a yellow blob fish sitting on mud with periscope eyes
rows.defect: the two separate sail-like dorsal fins are drawn as thin dark bristle tufts on the back — they read as stray hairs, not fins
rows.fix: replace the bristle tufts with two solid triangular dorsal sails, the front one taller, each with a visible fin membrane and 3-4 ray lines

rows.readsAs: a legless tan blob with two twigs on top
rows.defect: the oversized major claw is painted at the same tan as the carapace with no outline, so it merges into the body as a lump; the walking legs are all but absent (two tiny dark stubs), so nothing about the tile reads as a crab
rows.fix: darken the major claw a full step below carapace tone and give it a dark outline plus a visible pincer gape; draw four walking legs per side radiating out and down from the carapace edge
rows.verifyWhy: REFUTED — this was an over-read from a small tile. Both of the row's mustRead items are actually drawn and legible at size: the left claw is a large oval chela with an open two-finger pincer, plainly several times the volume of the small right claw with its own tiny pincer (grossly unequal, as the note demands), and two dark eye stalks stand clearly up off the carapace with eye beads on top. The auditor's 'two twigs on top' are the stalked eyes — a correct feature misread as debris. Real but sub-FAIL defects: the major claw is the same tan value as the carapace with no outline so it lumps into the body silhouette, and the walking legs are three hairline dark strokes per side that nearly vanish. Raise the claw's edge contrast and thicken the legs; the identity reads.

rows.readsAs: a snail with a coiled shell and eye tentacles
a spotted brown reef fish
rows.defect: the huge cavernous mouth with a jutting lower jaw — the grouper's whole identity — is not drawn at all; the head ends in a plain closed snout, and the caudal fin is a blocky brown rectangle rather than a rounded paddle
rows.fix: cut a wide mouth line back past the eye with the lower jaw protruding beyond the upper; round the caudal fin's trailing edge into a fan

rows.readsAs: a green crab with spidery legs
rows.defect: the two claws are thin sticks with tiny pincers held up above the carapace like antennae instead of heavy unequal crusher claws, and the rear legs are the same thin sticks with no paddle tips
rows.fix: thicken the chelipeds to ~2.5x current width, make one visibly larger than the other, and hold them forward at carapace level; flatten and widen the last leg segment on the rearmost pair into a paddle

rows.readsAs: a grey finless sea mammal with a fluked tail
rows.defect: the muzzle is a plain rounded body-end — the downturned bristly disc snout that separates a dugong from any other grey blimp is missing, and the body's horizontal wrinkle lines read as woodlouse segmentation

SPEC (reference/fauna.json:7845): aspect 3.5, eyes "small", mustRead = slender cigar-shaped body / narrow strap wings fringed with long hairs / asymmetrical cone-shaped rasping mouth. Two of three mustReads are wholly absent, the third is only nominal.

ROOT CAUSE the first auditor missed — Thrips IS the Bee. invertoverrides.ts:1035 `'Thrips': I({ hue:'#cdb464', abdomen:0.9, wings:'lace', antennae:'short' })` versus :1017 `'Bee': I({ hue:'#d4a017', abdomen:0.95, wings:'lace', antennae:'short', sting:true, fuzzy:true, pattern:'bands' })`. Thrips is the Bee spec minus sting/fuzz/bands in a paler gold. "Reads as a small yellow bee" is not an impression, it is the declaration.

CONFIRMED (a) different organism: three near-round tagmata, insectBody() half-axes head 0.78x0.70th, thorax 1.15x0.95th, abdomen abL*0.52=0.945th x 0.92th — the abdomen is literally a circle. Beaded silhouette confirmed structurally, not just visually.

CONFIRMED (b) defining trait absent, twice over. (i) FRINGE: grep for fringe/hair across invertoverrides.ts returns nothing in insectBody — the only `hairy` code is in arachnid() at :433. `wings:'lace'` is a quadratic blob at rgba(226,238,255,0.385) plus four venation strokes. Thysanoptera means "fringe wing"; the order's namesake trait has no code path. (ii) MOUTH: only `spec.proboscis` draws anything forward of the face and Thrips does not set it, so the head is one ellipse plus one eyeDot. The asymmetrical rasping cone is 100% absent.

CONFIRMED (c) visible drawing artifact, and now diagnosed: skin.ts:665 chitin packs 9 ring seams plus 9 pale lips into an abdomen only ~22 source px across (~2.4px spacing), and the wing venation strokes cross them the other way through a semi-opaque membrane. That moire IS the "cross-hatched mesh patch" — plainly visible even in the 300px tile.

AUDITOR OVERSTATEMENTS (wording only, finding stands): aspect is 2.8:1 not 2.5:1 (pixel-measured 2.73, code-derived 2.84 — still a clear miss of the 3.5 spec); wings are four translucent layers at alpha 0.385, not "two opaque blades" — they only stack to a near-opaque white mass; and all six leg roots ARE on the thorax in code (bx = cx-0.8th/+0.1th/+1.0th), but legs paint before the body so the roots hide and the hind pair's spread reaches cx+3.93th past the abdomen tip at cx+2.86th — so the on-screen read of "legs emerging behind the wing" is accurate even though the attachment is not. The front pair likewise visibly emerges from under the head.

Also against spec: eyeDot is th*0.24 on a head of half-height 0.70th, i.e. 34% of head height with a specular, where the reference asks for "small".

rows.fix: scale the bill to roughly 0.8x body length with a deep base tapering along a downward curve, band it with a dark tip and a contrasting stripe along the cutting edge, and paint a broad cream-yellow bib across the throat and upper breast plus a pale blue ring around the eye
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands; the size figure is corrected - the bill measures roughly 40-45% of body length, not a fifth. It is still a straight flat yellow cone with no downcurve and no colour banding, well short of 'nearly as long as the body' (mustRead 1). The vivid yellow-white bib (mustRead 2) and the bare blue eye-ring (mustRead 3) are both entirely absent, so the bird reads as a black waterfowl with a yellow bill. Damningly it is the same bill asset as the Hornbill tile - the two most distinctive bills in birds sharing one shape.

rows.readsAs: a black bird with a punk crest
rows.defect: the huge downcurved bill and its hollow casque are both absent - the bill is the same small straight yellow wedge used on the Toucan tile, and the spiky black tuft on the crown reads as hair, not a casque; the tail is a flat dark triangular flap pasted over the body edge
rows.fix: draw a long downcurved bill and mount a separate raised casque block along its top ridge running back to the forehead; replace the spike tuft with that casque, and draw a long broad banded tail as a layered feather group attached at the rump instead of a flat wedge
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed - the same body and the same small straight yellow bill as the Toucan tile. The huge downcurved bill and its hollow casque, both halves of mustRead 1, are absent; the spiky black tuft on the crown reads as a punk hair fringe, not a casque. No bare coloured throat or eye skin (mustRead 3). The tail is a flat dark triangular flap with a hard edge pasted over the body's right side rather than a long broad tail (mustRead 2).

rows.readsAs: a small green bird with a long thin beak
rows.defect: the needle bill and green iridescence read, but the bird is a fat round body standing flat-footed on the ground with folded wings - there is no hover: the body should be near-vertical with blade-like wings blurred beside it and the feet tucked
rows.fix: rotate the body toward vertical, tuck the feet up against the belly, replace the folded wing with a pair of narrow swept blades drawn at low opacity to read as motion, and add a bright iridescent gorget patch at the throat

rows.readsAs: a kingfisher
rows.defect: the head is a small ball perched on a visible neck above a large round body, when the diagnostic is an oversized head with no visible neck at all; the tail is a flat stiff dark blue wedge sticking out horizontally with a hard straight edge
rows.fix: enlarge the head to about 0.4 of body height and seat it directly on the shoulders so no neck gap shows, and shorten the tail to a stubby feather group with a softened outline

rows.readsAs: a brown bird with loose feathers stuck to it
rows.defect: the wing and tail are separate flat blades floating off the body - a straight sliver crossing the left body edge and a loose fan of unattached feather shapes to the right that read as pasted leaves; the beak is a small flat yellow wedge with no hook and no cere, and there is no brow ridge and no feathered legs
rows.fix: attach the folded wing as one shape anchored at the shoulder and lying along the flank to the tail tip with feather splits as internal lines; hook the beak tip down into a point and add a fleshy cere at its base plus a dark bony brow bar over the eye; thicken the legs with feathering to the ankle above the talons
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed at 5x zoom - the worst artifact in the set. A straight dark wing blade crosses the left of the body and projects into empty space with no shoulder join, and on the right a fan of five separate feather lozenges floats clear of the body with visible gaps, reading as pasted leaves. The beak is a small flat yellow wedge with no hook and no cere (mustRead 1); no bony brow ridge (mustRead 2); the legs are bare yellow sticks ending in a splayed flat paddle, not massive feathered legs with talons (mustRead 3).

rows.readsAs: an owl
a green rubber ring with a head stuck on
rows.defect: the body is one closed torus with no overlapping coils and no visible tail tip, and the head is a small pale oval pasted on the right side of the ring with a hard light rim and no neck continuity; the dark oval blotches are absent - the skin has only faint pale specks
rows.fix: draw the snake as a continuous tapering tube that crosses over itself at least twice with a visible tail tip so the coils overlap; grow the head out of the neck at the same width and taper it forward rather than compositing a separate ellipse; paint large dark olive oval blotches in two staggered rows along the back
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands with two corrections: the body IS massively thick (mustRead 1 is met, not missed), and there is a faint inner coil rather than a perfectly closed torus. What holds it at FAIL is the head - a small pale oval with a hard light rim pasted onto the right of the ring with no neck continuity, a clear composite seam at size - plus mustRead 3, the dark oval blotches over olive-green skin, which is absent, leaving only faint pale specks. Same asset as Boa and Python.

rows.readsAs: a tan doughnut with a head stuck on
rows.defect: same closed-torus body as the Anaconda tile; the head is a round pasted oval with a hard grey rim instead of a heavy arrow-shaped head, there is no dark eye stripe, and the saddle-shaped dorsal blotches are missing - only faint pale dots remain
rows.fix: widen the head into a triangle behind the eyes and blend it into the neck, add a dark bar running from the eye back to the jaw corner, and paint dark saddle blotches across the back that redden toward the tail
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. Identical torus and identical pasted round head with a hard grey rim as Anaconda and Python, recoloured tan. Two of three mustReads absent: no saddle-shaped dorsal blotches reddening toward the tail (only faint pale dots), and no heavy arrow-shaped head with a dark eye stripe - the head is a plain ellipse with a cartoon slit eye. Three snakes on one asset is itself the failure.

rows.readsAs: a plain tan coil with a head stuck on
rows.defect: the head is the same pasted oval with a hard grey outline as Boa and Anaconda, and the net-like geometric blotch pattern - the one thing that makes it a python - is entirely absent, leaving a plain tan tube with faint dots
rows.fix: paint a reticulated pattern: a lattice of dark lines enclosing lighter irregular cells running the length of the body; add a row of small pale pits along the upper and lower lip, and blend the head into the neck instead of compositing an ellipse
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands; one correction - this tile DOES show a visible tail tip, a small hooked taper terminating inside the inner coil, so 'no tail tip' is wrong here. It fails on mustRead 1: the net-like geometric blotched pattern, the single thing that identifies a python, is entirely absent, leaving a plain tan tube with faint dots. No heat-sensing pit row (mustRead 2). Head is the same pasted hard-rimmed oval as Boa and Anaconda.

rows.readsAs: a green frog-lizard with no tail
rows.defect: there is no tail at all - the body ends in a hard-edged pointed wedge just behind the hind leg; the back armour is a panel of ruled vertical lines rather than raised scutes, and the head is a rounded snout with a curved smile line and one slit eye, so it reads amphibian
rows.fix: add a tail at least as long as the head and body, tapering and laterally flattened; replace the ruled panel with individual raised scute blocks in rows down the back and neck; flatten and broaden the snout into a rounded shovel with a straight jaw line and a bony ridge between the eyes
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. There is no tail at all - the body terminates in a hard-edged pointed wedge immediately behind the hind leg, which for a crocodilian is a defining trait absent AND a visible truncation artifact. Measured aspect is roughly 1.5 against the reference's 4.5. The back armour is a panel of ruled vertical lines, not raised scutes (mustRead 2); no bony ridge between the eyes (mustRead 1); the head is a rounded snout with a curved smile line and a single slit eye, so the whole thing reads amphibian.

rows.readsAs: a crocodile
rows.defect: the tail is a flat triangular wedge with straight top and bottom edges ending in a sharp point - no double crest, no thickness - and the whole body reads as a flat cardboard cutout of ruled vertical lines in pale gold rather than an armoured olive animal
rows.fix: lengthen the tail to about half total length and give it a serrated double crest along the top that merges into a single crest at the rear; break the ruled body lines into individual scute blocks and darken the base colour to olive-brown with a paler belly

rows.readsAs: a green frog
rows.defect: the round adhesive toe discs - the diagnostic feature - are absent: the toes are thin bare spikes; the hind legs are straight sticks splayed sideways instead of folded into tight Z-shapes, and the eyes are plain black rather than red
rows.fix: cap every toe with a distinct round pad noticeably wider than the toe, fold each hind leg into a Z (thigh up, shin back, foot forward) so the knee rises above the body line, and colour the iris red with a vertical pupil

rows.readsAs: a red ladybird or jellybean
rows.defect: there is no frog anatomy: the head is not separable from the body, both eyes are crammed into the upper-right corner of a single red blob facing the same way, the mouth is a hard-edged black cavity beside them, and the limbs are four tiny nubs at the bottom corners
rows.fix: build it as a real frog at small scale - a distinct head with a rounded blunt snout, two jet-black eyes set symmetrically on top of the skull and bulging above the outline, a smooth body, and four visible limbs with the hind pair folded - then paint bold contrasting blotches over the warning colour
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. There is no frog anatomy: the head is not separable from the body, both eyes are crammed together into the upper-right of a single red blob facing the same way, and a hard-edged black cavity sits beside them as a mouth. Limbs are four tiny nubs at the bottom corners - no haunches, no long hind legs. mustRead 3 (rounded blunt snout) is absent and the eye placement is a visible construction defect. The vivid warning colour and blotches are the only things that land; a stranger names a ladybird.

rows.readsAs: a three-bead insect with sticks for legs
rows.defect: no leaf fragment is carried at all, the three body sections abut directly with no pinched petiole waist (and the gaster overlaps the thorax leaving a white seam arc), the antennae are two straight sticks with no elbow, there are no thoracic spines, and the front legs are short stubs ending in mid-air without reaching the ground
rows.fix: add a green leaf fragment held above the head in the mandibles at roughly head-to-thorax size; separate head, thorax and gaster with two narrow petiole nodes so the waist reads pinched; bend each antenna at a right angle a third of the way along; add two backward-pointing spines to the thorax; and draw six full three-segment legs all reaching the ground line
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. All three mustReads absent: no pinched petiole waist (the three beads abut directly, with a pale seam arc where the gaster overlaps the thorax), antennae are two straight bare sticks with no elbow, and there are neither thoracic spines nor any leaf fragment carried overhead. The front legs are short stubs terminating in mid-air well above the ground line, which is a visible drawing error at size. It does read as an ant, so it fails on absent traits rather than identity.

rows.readsAs: an ant with two orange leaves stuck on its back
rows.defect: the wings are two lobes mounted on the ABDOMEN, both swept back to one side, instead of two pairs spreading from the thorax; the white vein lines overshoot the wing edges and float in the background; the antennae are straight bare sticks with no clubs, the proboscis is missing, and the body is a chain of round balls
rows.fix: anchor all four wings to the thorax - forewing and hindwing on each side, spread symmetrically - and clip the vein strokes to the wing outline; end each antenna in a distinct swollen club; add a coiled watch-spring proboscis under the head; and slim the abdomen into a tapered segmented cone rather than a bead
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. The wings are two lobes mounted on the ABDOMEN and both swept to the same side, not two pairs spreading from the thorax (mustRead 1), on the same three-bead body as the Leafcutter Ant tile. The white vein lines overshoot the wing edges and float free in the background below-left - a genuine stroke-bleed artifact, unlike the Tiger and Okapi claims. Antennae are straight bare sticks with no clubs (mustRead 2) and the coiled proboscis (mustRead 3) is missing.

rows.readsAs: two brown balls on wire legs
rows.defect: legs sprout from the abdomen as well as the front section - spiders carry all eight legs on the cephalothorax only - and the legs are bare unjointed hairline sticks rather than thick densely hairy limbs; there are no fangs and no pedipalps, and only about six legs read
rows.fix: move every leg root onto the cephalothorax, draw eight legs in three visible segments each at roughly four times their current thickness with hair strokes bristling from the outline, add a pair of shorter leg-like pedipalps flanking the mouth, and hang two dark downward-stabbing fangs beneath the eye cluster
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. Legs sprout from the abdomen as well as the cephalothorax - about three per ball plus two stubs - which the reference note explicitly forbids ('the front section carries all eight legs'), and only about six legs read. The legs are bare unjointed hairline sticks, not the eight thick densely hairy legs of mustRead 1, and there are no fangs and no pedipalps (mustRead 3). It reads as two brown balls on wire.

rows.readsAs: pink chick with a yellow spoon stuck on its face
rows.defect: The spatulate bill and roseate colour read, but there is no neck at all — the head ball sits directly on the shoulder, so the tall wading silhouette the reference calls for is absent, and there is no bare face skin.
rows.fix: Insert a long slender neck column (about 0.8x body height) between head and body as on the Rhea painter, and lengthen the legs; leave the bill as-is, it is the best-read feature in the slice.

rows.readsAs: a pink baby chicken
rows.defect: All three mustReads are missing: the neck is absent (head on shoulder), the bill is a tiny straight yellow cone instead of a thick bill kinked sharply downward, and the legs are short bent chick legs rather than extremely long stilts. It is the Spoonbill body with the spoon removed.
rows.fix: Give the flamingo its own silhouette: neck length ~1.2x body drawn as an S, bill drawn as a pale wedge with a black down-bent distal half, legs at least 1.5x body height with a visible backward-bending ankle joint.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds at size. The head is welded to the shoulder with zero neck, the bill is a small straight yellow cone with no downward kink, and the legs are ordinary short bent bird legs, not stilts. All three mustReads (S-neck, bent bill, extremely long legs) are absent; the silhouette is the same generic round-bodied bird asset used for Bustard/Sandgrouse/Sparrow, just pink. A stranger says 'pink chick'.

rows.readsAs: a green mushroom-topped table with a turtle head
rows.defect: The shell is a dome sitting on a flat slab with the four legs drawn as straight untapered rectangular posts — the reference's exact named failure. Only two legs read; a small leaf-shaped flipper hovers unattached beside the neck.
rows.fix: Replace the post legs with short tapering scaly stumps whose tops disappear under the shell rim, and delete the free-floating flipper shape near the neck or attach it to the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a golden goldfish
rows.defect: No barbels anywhere at the mouth corners — the single most carp-specific trait — and the dorsal fin is a small bump over the mid-back rather than a long fin running most of the back.
rows.fix: Add two pairs of short drooping whiskers at the corners of the mouth, and extend the dorsal fin base to cover roughly 60% of the topline instead of a 15% bump.

rows.readsAs: a grey deep-bodied panfish
rows.defect: The spiny dorsal is a flat grey sawtooth band whose straight base line does not follow the curved back, so the three front spikes hover clear of the body; it also covers only the rear half of the back instead of the whole back.
rows.fix: Anchor the spine bases to the actual dorsal curve so no gap opens at the front, extend the fin from just behind the head to the tail, and tint it from the body colour instead of flat grey.

rows.readsAs: a deep silver fish with fangs
rows.defect: The teeth hang down from the upper jaw along a straight lower head edge; the undershot jutting lower jaw that defines a piranha is absent, and the head tapers to a point rather than showing the steep blunt forehead.
rows.fix: Push the lower jaw forward past the snout tip and set the triangular teeth on it pointing up, and steepen the forehead from the eye to the mouth so the profile is blunt rather than lemon-pointed.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy capybara or a woolly cow
rows.defect: No horns at all, no shoulder hump (the topline is level and the head is carried high, the opposite of a bison), and no beard. A pale rectangular patch of coat-skin shows as a seam over the shoulder, and the mouth line juts out past the tip of the muzzle as a stray stroke.
rows.fix: Raise the topline into a hump peaking over the forelegs and drop the head below the shoulder line; add short black upcurved horns and a chin/throat beard; clip the mouth stroke to the muzzle outline and fix the shoulder coat seam.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. No horns of any kind, and a hornless bison is not a bison. The topline is level and the head is carried ABOVE it — the exact inverse of the front-heavy hump-to-small-hips silhouette the reference calls out as the trait most often lost. No beard. A pale wedge of coat-skin shows as a seam over the shoulder and a stray mouth stroke runs out past the muzzle tip. 0/3 mustReads.

rows.readsAs: a plump tan burrowing rodent
a rabbit
rows.defect: Ears and high-set eye read well, but the very long powerful hind legs are just two small brown nubs poking below a round body — a jackrabbit's defining leggy hindquarters are absent.
rows.fix: Draw a large angled hind limb: thick thigh mass merging into the rump, long tibia, and a long foot on the ground, so the rump sits visibly higher than the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a tree squirrel
rows.defect: The tail is a smooth thick sausage with a pale highlight stripe arched high over the back (tree-squirrel plume position) and the ears are pointed tufts — the reference explicitly calls for a short thin flat tail and tiny ears. The body is a ball, not the long low tube of aspect 2.4.
rows.fix: Shorten the tail to ~40% of body length, drop it to trail behind at body height, give it a sparse hair fringe instead of a smooth tube, and shrink the ears to low rounded bumps.

rows.readsAs: a brown hamster
rows.defect: Identical silhouette to the Prairie Dog tile in a different hue. The incisors are the shared tiny white block at the lip line, not huge protruding orange incisors, and the forefeet have no digging claws at all.
rows.fix: Recolour and enlarge the incisor pair to orange chisels that project clearly forward of the lip, and add three or four splayed pale claws to each forefoot nub.

rows.readsAs: a streaky brown crested ground bird
a coiled ribbed hose with a bead stuck on the end
rows.defect: The head is a plain rounded ellipse pasted onto the body end with its own visible pale rim — no triangular pit-viper skull, no thin neck, no reared S. The body is drawn with regular ring ribs that read as an earthworm rather than scales. The rattle is present but tiny.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse head with a wide arrow-shaped wedge that narrows into a distinctly thinner neck, blend the head into the neck with no rim stroke, rear the front third off the coil, and enlarge the tail rattle to 3-4 stacked segments.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. The head is a plain rounded ellipse butted onto the body end with its own pale rim seam — no triangular pit-viper skull, no thin neck, no reared S (2/3 mustReads absent). The body is drawn with evenly spaced ring ribs that read as earthworm annuli rather than scales. The rattle is genuinely present and segmented, so mustRead 1 passes, but the animal still reads as a ribbed hose.

rows.readsAs: a spiky spotted pancake lizard
rows.defect: Body disc, flank fringe and skull horns all read. The tail, however, is a long thick smooth tan arc curled up over the left flank — as big as the body and reading as a separate trunk-like limb, where a horned lizard has a tiny stub.
rows.fix: Cut the tail to a short flat triangular stub at the rear rim of the disc and remove the upward curl; also angle the skull spikes backward rather than up.

rows.readsAs: a green lacewing or midge
rows.defect: The huge angled jumping hind legs — the first mustRead — are absent; all six legs are identical thin straight sticks and the two middle ones end in mid-air. The antennae are long thin filaments (a cricket trait) instead of short stout ones.
rows.fix: Give the hind pair a thick swollen femur that rises above the wing line and cranks down to a long spined tibia, shorten the antennae to stubby segmented rods, and land the mid legs on the ground plane.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. The first mustRead — huge angled hind legs rising above the back — is simply not drawn: all six legs are identical thin straight sticks with no femur, and the two middle ones terminate in mid-air above the ground line (a visible drawing artifact). Antennae are long thin filaments. Reads as a lacewing/midge.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown cricket
rows.defect: Long antennae and the flat wings over a rounded back read correctly, but the jumping hind legs are thin bent wires with no femur mass, and the mid legs stop in empty air short of the ground.
rows.fix: Thicken the hind femur into a visible teardrop at the body, and extend the mid legs to touch the shadow ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a three-lump insect, probably an ant
rows.defect: The three body lumps read, but the antennae are two straight bristles with no elbow, the rear legs spring from the abdomen ball instead of the thorax, and the abdomen is a lighter striped disc with a bright rim that reads as pasted on.
rows.fix: Bend each antenna at a sharp mid-joint, move all six leg roots onto the middle segment, and drop the abdomen rim stroke and match its tone to the thorax.

rows.readsAs: two balls with sticks poking out of them
rows.defect: Several legs on the right spring directly from the abdomen — the exact violation the reference forbids — and two legs stick straight up out of the tops of both body sections like antennae. Legs are straight rods with no up-then-down arch, and the abdomen is a rimmed pasted disc.
rows.fix: Root all eight legs on the cephalothorax only, in four pairs; give each a raised knee so the leg arches above the body then descends to the ground; delete the two vertical spars on the dorsal surface.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, and it violates the reference's explicit prohibition. Legs on the right spring directly from the abdomen, and one leg on each body section points straight UP out of the top like an antenna. Legs are straight rods with no up-then-down arch. The abdomen is a pasted disc with its own bright rim. 2/3 mustReads fail, one of them the one the note singles out as never-do.

rows.readsAs: a white goat with straight ringed horns
rows.defect: The ringed vertical horns and pale coat carry a saiga-ish read, but the muzzle is a straight tapering goat snout — the bulbous drooping trunk-like nose that is the saiga's whole identity is absent. rows.fix: Swell the front third of the muzzle into a downward-hanging bulb that overhangs the mouth with two nostrils on its underside; clip the mouth stroke to the muzzle silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a llama with a lump falling off its backside
rows.defect: A large pale-tan ellipse sits outside the body silhouette at the rump, floating over the tail plume — a detached haunch disc. The stiff upright brush mane is missing (only a small dark triangle on the forehead), the neck is long and slender rather than stocky, and the mouth stroke juts past the muzzle.
rows.fix: Clip the haunch ellipse to the body path so it cannot render beyond the rump outline, and add an erect brush mane as a row of short dark bristles along the whole neck crest.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. A large pale-tan ellipse sits outside the body contour at the rump, overlapping the tail brush — an unmistakable detached haunch disc, a hard artifact. The stiff erect brush mane is absent (only a dark forelock triangle), the neck is long and slender instead of stocky, and a mouth stroke juts past the muzzle. Reads as a llama. 0/3 mustReads.

rows.readsAs: a pale fawn or young llama
rows.defect: The ears are fused into a single flat grey mushroom cap sitting on the crown — no pair of long upright ears reads, which is the one trait that makes a wild ass a wild ass. There is also no erect mane, and the mouth stroke juts past the muzzle tip.
rows.fix: Replace the cap with two separate ears, each about half the head length, narrow, upright and dark-rimmed with a pale inner surface; add a short bristle mane along the neck crest.
rows.verifyWhy: Defect confirmed, description slightly overstated: two ears ARE drawn, but they overlap into one short rounded grey cap. Either way the defining trait — very long upright ears — is absent, and so is the erect mane (2/3 mustReads gone). The tufted tail is actually good. The mouth line is a ruled stroke across the whole jaw. Still reads as a pale fawn/llama, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a camel
rows.defect: Hump, high curving neck and long legs all read. The hump is drawn as a flat untextured tan dome pasted on top of the shaggy coat with a hard edge, and the coat patch itself shows an elliptical seam at the shoulder and haunch.
rows.fix: Paint the hump with the same coat texture as the body and blend its base into the topline instead of an overlapping dome; feather the coat-patch edges.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy ox wearing a curled ram horn over one eye
rows.defect: The horn is a near-complete cream ring drawn across the face, overlapping the eye and muzzle — an obvious pasted spiral, and wrong shape for a yak. A pale ellipse also floats outside the rump over the tail plume. The head is carried high instead of low.
rows.fix: Swap the ram spiral for two simple horns emerging from the top of the skull behind the eye, sweeping out then up; clip the haunch ellipse inside the body path; drop the head so the muzzle sits below the shoulder line.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. The horn is a near-closed cream ring pasted across the face, overlapping both the eye and the muzzle — an obvious drawing artifact and the wrong horn shape entirely (it is the same pasted spiral the Goat wears). A pale ellipse also floats outside the rump over the tail plume. The flank curtain is good and the tail plume is good, but the artifact alone fails it.

rows.readsAs: a sandy rabbit
rows.defect: Drawn as a quadruped blob: the stilt-like hind legs are two small brown nubs, the tail is a short smooth arc about half the body length with no black-and-white tuft, and the eye is a small dot rather than huge and round. Only the ears are right.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a biped — hind limbs three to four times the forelimbs with the body tilted upright and the tiny forelegs tucked at the chest; make the tail longer than the body and end it in a two-tone tuft; enlarge the eye to roughly a third of head height.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. It is the shared rabbit-blob template: hind legs are two small brown nubs, not stilts several times the forelimbs; the tail is a short smooth arc with no black-and-white tuft; the eye is a small dot despite eyes:'prominent'. A rimmed pale disc shows on the haunch. 3/3 mustReads absent — only the ears read.

rows.readsAs: a golden hamster
a quail chick
rows.defect: The body is a low round ball on short bent legs with a stubby neck — the opposite of a bustard's heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs above a thick upright neck. rows.fix: Roughly double the leg length and make them bare and grey-tan, raise the body clear of the ground into a horizontal carriage, and add a thick vertical neck about half body height carrying a flat-crowned head.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, and the duplicate claim verified: I rendered Bustard, Sandgrouse and Sparrow side by side and they are the same bird asset at different scale and tint. Low round ball body, short bent legs, stubby neck, tiny pointed cone bill — the opposite of a heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs under a thick upright neck. 3/3 mustReads absent.

rows.readsAs: a plump short-legged desert ground bird
a coiled grey vacuum hose
rows.defect: The head is a flat rimmed ellipse butted onto the body with a visible seam, and the body is a thick ring-ribbed doughnut — no trace of the whip-thin slender body in a fast S-curve, and the ribbing reads as segmented worm rather than smooth glossy scales.
rows.fix: Halve the body thickness and lay it out as an open S rather than a closed coil, remove the transverse ribbing in favour of a smooth glossy gradient, and taper the head out of the neck instead of pasting an ellipse on it.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. Reference aspect is 5 (whip-thin) in a crawling S; this is a thick coiled doughnut with regular ring ribs that read as segmented worm, not smooth glossy scales. The head is a flat ellipse butted on with a visible pale rim seam. 2/3 mustReads absent plus a seam artifact.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon blue platypus or newt
rows.defect: The head is a pale-blue ellipse with a bright rim pasted onto the body with a visible seam, and the mouth is a ruled straight line that runs past the back of the head. rows.fix: Build the head as a wedge that tapers out of the neck — wide at the jaw hinge, narrowing to the snout — with no rim stroke; end the mouth line at the jaw hinge; give four sprawled legs bent at elbow and knee that lift the belly clear of the shadow.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. The head is a pale ellipse with a bright rim pasted onto the body at a visible seam, and the mouth is a ruled straight line that runs clear past the back of the head — a hard artifact. The belly rests on the ground on two dark stubs, so 'sprawled legs with the belly held clear' is absent, and the head is rounded rather than blunt-triangular. 2/3 mustReads gone.

rows.readsAs: a fox on stilts
rows.defect: The leggy silhouette and red coat read well. The ears are a single dark faceted origami polygon on the crown rather than two large erect triangles; the legs are uniform orange with no black stockings; the mane is only a dark patch on the head, not along neck and shoulders.
