rows.readsAs: a blobfish
rows.defect: The caudal fin is a dark brown fan separated from the body by a clear gap of background, so the tail floats free; a faint stray stroke runs from the fan into the body.
rows.fix: Join the fan to the body at a short peduncle and tone it to the pink body colour instead of dark brown; delete the stray stroke.

rows.readsAs: a dark rod with belly lights — the same picture as the Dragonfish tile
rows.defect: The enormous pelican pouch mouth, which is the entire identity of this animal, is absent: the head end is a blunt tube with a few small teeth. The tail is a small fan rather than a whip tapering to a luminous tip.
rows.fix: Balloon the jaw into a loose pouch several times deeper than the body, hinged well back behind the pinhead eyes at the very tip of the snout, and taper the rear half into a thin whip ending in a small light.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds up. The pelican pouch mouth is the entire identity of this animal and it is simply not drawn - the head end is a blunt tube with a few small teeth. The whip tail tapering to a luminous tip is a small fan instead, and the eye is a white ring set back from the snout rather than a pinhead at the tip. 0 of 3 mustReads; what remains is a dark rod with a row of cyan belly photophores, which is the generic deep-sea template.

rows.readsAs: a fat green parrot with a plain ring stamped on its side
rows.defect: The folded wing is a bare pale circle outlined on the flank and a separate green sphere sits off the rump — both read as pasted discs, not feathers; the owl-like whiskered facial disc is entirely absent (plain green head, small yellow beak).
rows.fix: Replace the circular wing decal with a layered covert/primary group that follows the body contour and merges into the flank, delete the free-floating rump sphere, and add the facial disc: a pale radiating whisker ruff around the eye plus the large pale hooked kakapo bill instead of the small yellow one.
rows.verifyWhy: Species-misread claim REFUTED: at size it reads as a heavy squat mottled-green flightless parrot, i.e. a kakapo (mustReads 1 and 3 both land — the plumage is genuinely mottled dark/light green with yellow highlights). But the two artifacts are real and worse at 6x: the flank 'wing' is a hard-edged circle with a rim and a speckle fill that does not match the surrounding feather pass — it reads as a stamped disc or a hole — and the rump carries a flat untextured pale-green ellipse half-outside the silhouette. The owl-like whiskered facial disc (mustRead 2, the trait behind the name 'owl parrot') is absent; the head is plain green. Visible construction artifact + one absent defining trait = FAIL, but on narrower grounds than stated.

rows.readsAs: a black sheep or musk-ox calf
rows.defect: Coat is long shaggy grey-black wool when the sun bear's mustRead is a short SLEEK jet-black coat; the golden-cream crescent chest patch is missing entirely, and no claws are drawn on the dark blob feet.
rows.fix: Set the coat to short-pile sleek black (no shag/fringe pass), paint the horseshoe crescent in golden-cream across the upper chest, and give the forefeet long pale curved climbing claws so the silhouette stops reading as a hoofed animal.
rows.verifyWhy: Fully upheld and if anything understated. The coat is long shaggy grey-white wool over a dark head and dark legs — the exact Suffolk-sheep pattern — against a mustRead of 'short sleek jet-black coat'. The golden-cream chest crescent is absent. A stranger names a sheep, not the smallest bear. Only correction: small white claw tips ARE drawn at the toes, so 'no claws' is wrong; they are far too short for 'very long curved climbing claws'. Two of three mustReads absent plus a different-organism read.

rows.readsAs: a sandy dog
rows.defect: The two erect triangular ears are fused into one flat dark wedge sitting like a cap on the crown, the muzzle is painted in a cold blue-grey that does not belong on a sandy-ginger canid, and the white feet are missing (feet are dark).
rows.fix: Split the ear into two separate erect triangles with visible inner-ear shading and daylight between them, retint the muzzle to a warm ginger-brown, and add white socks on all four feet plus a white tail tip.

rows.readsAs: a white chicken with a small tuft
rows.defect: The bill is a small straight yellow-orange cone; the mustRead is a heavy DARK hooked bill, which is the parrot cue. The crest exists but is a thin white wisp rather than a raised fan.
rows.fix: Swap the bill to a broad dark-grey hooked parrot bill with a visible cere, and widen the crest into a fan of 5-6 recurved sulphur-yellow plumes.

rows.readsAs: a glowing beetle
a generic brown bat
rows.defect: The flat pig-like nose pad — the single feature that separates this from any other bat — is absent (plain short snout), and the wing membranes are built from straight-edged triangular facets so they read as folded paper rather than skin.
rows.fix: Add the flat circular nose pad with two slit nostrils on the muzzle tip, and curve the wing membrane between the finger struts (concave trailing edge) instead of straight chords; add the long thumb claw at the wrist bend.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown bear, but the head cues a ram at thumbnail size
rows.defect: The ear is an oversized dark solid disc set high on the skull, which at small size reads as the base of a curled horn; the muzzle is a dark teardrop pasted over a lighter face plate, and the dished concave profile and long pale front claws are both missing.
rows.fix: Shrink the ear to a small rounded semicircle set further back and tint it toward the coat, blend the muzzle into the face with a gradient rather than a hard edge, dish the profile between brow and nose, and draw 4-5 long pale claws on each forefoot.

rows.readsAs: a pale generic fish
rows.defect: Both defining traits are absent: the fins are small flat flaps with no fleshy muscular stalks, and the tail is a plain pointed flap instead of the three-lobed tail with the small central spike. The whole body is also washed out and semi-transparent.
rows.fix: Rebuild the paired fins as thick lobed paddles on visible muscular stalks standing clear of the body, and replace the caudal with the diphycercal three-lobe: upper lobe, lower lobe, and a small pointed epicaudal spike between them. Raise opacity and add white flecks on steel-blue.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld with one correction: it is not 'pale', it is very dark and low-contrast (steel-blue body, dark mottling) — the semi-transparency claim is right, the paleness claim is not. Both structural mustReads are genuinely absent at size: the fins are flat translucent flaps with no fleshy muscular stalks, and the tail is a plain rounded paddle with no three-lobed division and no central spike. Two of three defining traits missing; reads as a generic fish.

rows.readsAs: a plain cream ammonite shell
rows.defect: No tentacles and no leathery hood at the shell opening — the animal is missing altogether; the shell is uniform cream with no red-brown flame striping; and a pale translucent disc overlaps the lower-right of the shell as an unexplained artifact.
rows.fix: Draw the aperture with a dense fan of dozens of short suckerless tentacles plus the dark leathery hood above them, paint radial red-brown flame bands across the outer whorl fading to white on the underside, and remove the stray translucent disc.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld entirely. The shell is a well-drawn cream chambered coil with zero red-brown flame striping (mustRead 1 half-failed), and the ANIMAL is absent — no tentacle fan, no leathery hood (mustReads 2 and 3 both gone). The unexplained overlap is real and doubled: a faint translucent circle arc crosses the lower-right shell and a solid opaque grey ellipse sits on top of it, matching nothing anatomical. Reads as an empty ammonite shell.

rows.readsAs: a water bear
rows.defect: Body is saturated teal-cyan where the reference calls for translucent amber-tan with darker gut contents, and the stubby legs end in flat stumps with no claw bunches.
rows.fix: Retint to translucent amber-tan with a darker green-brown gut mass showing through the dorsal midline, and terminate each of the four leg pairs in a small splay of 3-4 curved claws, with the rear pair angled backward.

rows.readsAs: a horseshoe crab from above
rows.defect: The telson is a uniform hairline needle that reads like a pin stuck into the shell rather than a rigid tapering spike; the domed carapace also has no clear division into prosoma and hinged opisthosoma.
rows.fix: Give the tail real taper — thick at the hinge, narrowing to a point, roughly one third of the total length — and add the transverse hinge line with the row of short marginal spines on the rear shield.

rows.readsAs: a young deer
rows.defect: The horns are multi-tined branched antlers, not the pronghorn's single forward-hooked horn with one short anterior prong; and the body is uniform tan with no white throat bands and no white rump patch.
rows.fix: Replace the antler with a paired black horn that rises, hooks forward at the tip, and carries exactly one short forward prong halfway up; paint two white crescent bands across the throat and a large white rump patch.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, one claim REFUTED: at 8x each horn is a single beam with ONE short branching prong — structurally the pronghorn pattern, not 'multi-tined branched antlers'. What actually fails: the horns are cream/bone-colored and straight with no backward hook (they read as young antlers), and the coat is uniform tan with no white throat bands and no white rump patch — mustRead 2 absent outright. Those white marks are exactly what separates a pronghorn from a deer at a glance, so the different-organism read stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan antelope
rows.defect: The dark chocolate side stripe dividing tan from white is missing entirely, and the white face with its dark eye stripe is missing — the whole animal is one flat cream-tan. The lyre horns do read.
rows.fix: Paint the horizontal dark-brown flank band from shoulder to haunch with white below it and tan above, and add the white face blaze with a dark brown stripe running from eye to muzzle.

rows.readsAs: a red antelope with a black grid patch stuck on its shoulder
rows.defect: The vertical stripes are DARK/black instead of white, and they are confined to a hard-edged rectangular block over the neck and shoulder rather than running the length of the flank — the block reads as a pasted patch. The white chevron between the eyes is absent.
rows.fix: Recolour the stripes to cream-white, extend them as 10-14 thin vertical bands spaced evenly from shoulder to rump following the body curvature (no rectangular clip boundary), and add the white chevron across the face between the eyes.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld; the patch claim is vindicated at the FACE rather than the shoulder. The stripes are dark brown/black on chestnut — the diagnostic is TEN OR MORE WHITE stripes, so the key mustRead is inverted, not merely weak. Extent claim partly refuted: the striping actually covers most of the barrel, not a shoulder block; but it is bounded by hard straight bars (one long dark bar crosses the flank, another the neck) and a hard-edged rectangular striped block is pasted across the MUZZLE with stripes hanging off the jaw — a clear artifact. White chevron between the eyes absent. Horns are acceptable wavy spirals.

rows.readsAs: a small tan antelope
rows.defect: The forehead tuft is missing, and the diagnostic hunched posture is barely present — the topline is nearly level rather than arching to a rump higher than the shoulders.
rows.fix: Add a dark bristly crest tuft between the horn spikes, and raise the rump 8-12% above the shoulder with a rounded arched back so the crouching profile reads.

rows.readsAs: a giraffe-necked antelope
rows.defect: The huge ears are missing — only small nubs sit beside the horns, and the gerenuk's oversized ears are one of its three mustReads. There is also a visible tone seam where the pale rump meets the tan forequarters.
rows.fix: Enlarge the ears to roughly head-length, broad ovals held out sideways with pale inner surfaces, and blend the rump/shoulder tone transition into a gradient.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey goat-antelope
rows.defect: The coat is near-white rather than the bull's slate blue-grey, and the throat beard tuft is absent; the back also reads level instead of sloping down from high shoulders.
rows.fix: Retint the coat to desaturated slate blue-grey, hang a black bristle tuft from the mid-throat, and drop the rump line so the topline slopes visibly downward from the withers.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy-maned wild goat
a shaggy grizzled goat-antelope
rows.defect: The large donkey-like ears are missing — the ears are small nubs — and the head is narrow rather than heavy and blunt, so the serow's most distinctive head cue does not read.
rows.fix: Scale the ears up to long broad donkey ovals held out to the sides with pale inner surfaces, and widen the muzzle into a blunt heavy head.

rows.readsAs: a grey pigeon with plank wings
rows.defect: No split double crest, no black chest band over a white belly, feet are small yellow perching toes rather than enormous grey talons, and the bill is a tiny yellow cone instead of a massive hooked raptor beak. The spread wings are flat black planks with straight edges.
rows.fix: Add the divided pale-grey crest raised in two peaks, a heavy black hooked bill with yellow cere, a broad black band across the upper chest above a white belly, and oversized grey scaled feet with thick curved black talons; give the wings broad rounded fingered tips rather than straight planks.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld without reservation — the clearest FAIL in the set. All three mustReads absent: no split double crest (only a faint grey wisp), no black chest band over a white belly (uniform grey speckling), and the feet are small yellow perching toes rather than enormous grey talons. The bill is a tiny yellow triangle, not a massive hooked raptor beak, and the reference explicitly wants broad short forest wings — instead the wings are long straight dark planks extending far past the body on both sides. Reads as a grey dove.

rows.readsAs: a kingfisher
rows.defect: The dark brown eye stripe on a whitish head is missing — the head is uniform brown-grey — and the dagger bill is painted bright saturated yellow rather than the dark upper / pale lower mandible.
rows.fix: Lighten the head and nape to off-white, run a broad dark-brown band through the eye to the nape, and recolour the bill dark charcoal on top with a horn-white lower mandible.

rows.readsAs: a small crested brown gamebird
rows.defect: The bare blue face with a staring red eye is absent (plain brown face, dark eye), and the long broad tail is drawn as three thin separated straps rather than a broad fan.
rows.fix: Paint the facial skin bright cobalt blue with a red iris ringed dark, and merge the tail straps into one broad rounded fan with a pale buff terminal band.

rows.readsAs: a green bird with long tail streamers
rows.defect: The crimson belly is missing — the underside is the same green/pale as the back — so the bird's two-colour signature does not read.
rows.fix: Paint the breast and belly deep crimson from the lower throat back to the vent, keeping the emerald green on the head, back and wing coverts, with a clean white undertail.

rows.readsAs: a yellow canary or chick
rows.defect: The black face mask is absent — the head is plain yellow — and the bill is a small pointed orange cone rather than a thick conical seed-cracker, so the two traits that make it a masked weaver are both gone.
rows.fix: Add a solid black mask covering forehead, face and throat with a sharp boundary against the yellow, and thicken the bill into a short deep black cone.

rows.readsAs: a grey-brown goose or guineafowl
rows.defect: The thin curved forehead horn — the single diagnostic of the horned screamer — is completely absent, and there are no bony spurs at the wing bends.
rows.fix: Add a long thin pale quill-like horn projecting forward and upward from the centre of the forehead, and a pair of sharp bony spurs at the carpal joint of each wing.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld after an 8x check of the crown specifically: the forehead is a plain smooth dome — the thin curved horn is not there, faint or otherwise, and there are no bony wing spurs. Two of three mustReads absent, including the single namesake diagnostic of the horned screamer; without it the bird is a guineafowl. This is the mildest FAIL of the seventeen — the body, bill and posture are right and there is no artifact — but a namesake trait being wholly absent meets the bar.

rows.readsAs: a ribbed clam or scallop shell
rows.defect: The towering dorsal and anal fins are missing entirely — there is only a small dark ridge on top — so nothing reads as a fish; the heavy horizontal rib texture reinforces the shell impression. The frilled rear rudder and tall body are correct.
rows.fix: Add the two enormous triangular fins, dorsal and anal, each roughly as tall as the body is deep and set opposite each other at the rear third, and replace the concentric rib texture with fine mottled leathery skin.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld. The silhouette-defining mustRead — towering dorsal AND anal fins top and bottom — is reduced to one small dark stub above the eye with nothing at all below, so the outline is a closed oval. Combined with heavy horizontal rib banding across the whole disc, the honest read is a scallop or clam shell with an eye painted on. The auditor's own concessions (tall body, rear rudder) are fair, which makes the missing fins the whole of the failure — but they are the whole of the animal's outline.

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or young barracuda
rows.defect: The ridged oval sucker plate on top of the head is absent — that plate is the whole identity of a remora — leaving a featureless dark torpedo.
rows.fix: Draw a flat oval plate on the dorsal surface of the head running from snout to behind the eye, filled with 16-20 transverse lamellae ridges and outlined by a raised rim; also jut the lower jaw past the upper.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld. The slim dark torpedo (mustRead 2) is right; the ridged oval sucker plate on top of the head is absent — the only candidate is a faint pale band running along the mid-flank, unridged and in the wrong place, which does not read as a sucker. mustRead 3 also drifts: the fins sit forward, not far back. The reference calls the sucker the modified dorsal that defines the fish; without it this is a needlefish. Also very dim and low-contrast against the background.

rows.readsAs: a generic yellow sunfish or perch
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail: the topline is a smooth convex curve instead of the flat straight slope to an upturned mouth, the bold black wedge bars are absent (uniform gold body), and the spiky dorsal fin sits mid-back rather than far back near the tail.
rows.fix: Flatten the dorsal profile into a straight line from snout to dorsal origin and tip the mouth upward at the end of it, move the dorsal fin back to sit above the anal fin near the caudal peduncle, and paint 4-5 black wedge bars widening downward on a silver flank.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, with one softening: the spiky dorsal is set over the rear third — not truly 'mid-back', so that sub-claim is overstated, though still not 'far back near the tail'. The other two mustReads fail outright at size: the topline is a smooth convex dome instead of the flat straight slope to an upturned mouth, and the body is uniform gold with faint stipple where the bold black wedge bars — the archerfish's whole visual signature — should be. Reads as a generic sunfish/perch.

rows.readsAs: a dark ribbon-shaped fish
rows.defect: The undulating anal ribbon fin is a one-pixel hairline along the belly instead of a deep rippling ribbon, and the body ends in a blunt rounded stub rather than tapering to a blade-thin point.
rows.fix: Widen the ventral ribbon fin to roughly 15% of body depth and give it a wave along its edge, and taper the last third of the body smoothly to a fine point with no caudal flare.

rows.readsAs: a pale pike-like fish
rows.defect: The skin carries a regular diamond scale pattern although the icefish is explicitly scaleless, and the large fan pectoral fins are reduced to small flaps.
rows.fix: Remove the scale tiling and replace it with smooth translucent skin showing faint internal structure (gill arches, spine shadow), and enlarge the pectorals into broad rounded fans with visible ray lines.

rows.readsAs: a small brown minnow
rows.defect: No dorsal fin is drawn at all — the topline is smooth — although the mustRead specifically calls for a dorsal set far back close to the tail.
rows.fix: Add a small rounded dorsal fin positioned just ahead of the caudal peduncle, mirroring the anal fin below, and round the paddle-shaped pectorals slightly more.

rows.readsAs: a spotted fish with a translucent halo behind it
rows.defect: The pectoral fans are drawn as a large semi-transparent ovoid layered BEHIND the body and rising above the dorsal line, so they read as a ghost halo rather than wings hinged at the pectoral base; the electric blue appears only as scattered spots, not as the fin edging.
rows.fix: Anchor the fan at a visible pectoral joint behind the gill cover, fan the rays outward and downward from that point in front of the body, and run a bright electric-blue band along the outer margin of the fin instead of spotting the interior.

rows.readsAs: metal chimneys on a rock
rows.defect: The tunic is painted as opaque brushed-metal silver with a hard panel grid, so the translucent tunic showing the internal basket is completely missing and the object reads as industrial rather than living.
rows.fix: Retint to a translucent yellow-pink jelly with soft internal shading, show the dark pharyngeal basket and gut through the wall, and replace the metallic panel grid with irregular soft surface wrinkles.

rows.readsAs: a chain of opaque blue beans
rows.defect: Each zooid is a solid opaque navy body — the salp's defining glassy transparency and its openings at both ends are missing — and there is no coloured gut nucleus inside.
rows.fix: Drop opacity so the background shows through each barrel, open both ends as visible rims, keep the pale muscle hoops as bright bands on the near wall only, and add a small orange-brown gut nucleus inside each individual.

rows.readsAs: a pink speckled tube
rows.defect: The bioluminescent glow is hot magenta-pink where the reference calls for a cold blue glow, so the colour reads as a lava lamp rather than a deep-sea colony.
rows.fix: Retint the tube and its emitted glow to cold cyan-blue at low saturation, keep the pale zooid speckles slightly brighter than the wall, and darken the sealed end so the open end reads.

rows.readsAs: an earthworm or maggot with one googly eye
rows.defect: It has a blunt rounded head bearing a single large black eye, which the reference explicitly forbids (no head, no eyes); the body is an opaque cream ringed tube rather than a translucent blade pointed at both ends, and the V-shaped muscle chevrons and oral tentacle fringe are absent.
rows.fix: Delete the eye and head bulge, taper both ends to points to give a flattened blade silhouette, drop opacity and draw a row of nested V-chevrons along the flank plus the dark notochord line end to end, and fringe the front opening with fine oral cirri.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld; the reference is explicit ('no head, no jaws and no eyes') and the art draws a bulbous rounded head with a black eye dot on it — a forbidden feature, not merely a missing one. All three mustReads fail: the body is opaque cream and ring-segmented rather than translucent and blade-pointed at both ends, no V-shaped muscle chevrons, no oral tentacle fringe. Only correction: the eye is a small dot, not 'one large googly eye'. Reads as an earthworm.

rows.readsAs: a harvestman or daddy-long-legs
rows.defect: The body is two fat bulbous spheres — the exact opposite of the pycnogonid's mustRead, a body reduced to a thin stick between the legs — and the long tubular sucking proboscis is missing entirely; the leg bases also do not visibly meet the trunk.
rows.fix: Replace the two globes with a narrow segmented rod barely wider than a leg, attach each of the four leg pairs at a visible lateral process along that rod, and project a long straight tubular proboscis forward from the front end beneath the four-eye turret.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, with a partial refutation: four black eyes ARE drawn in a 2x2 cluster on the front sphere, matching the reference note about the eye turret, and the leg bases do converge on the body acceptably. But mustRead 1 is inverted rather than merely missed — the reference demands a body 'reduced to a thin stick between the legs' and the art gives two fat bulbous spheres — and the long tubular sucking proboscis is absent. Reads as a harvestman.

rows.readsAs: a pale grub or generic shrimp
rows.defect: The body is opaque cream with two bulbous carapace-like lobes although the fairy shrimp has NO carapace and is a bare translucent tube; the eleven pairs of leaf-like swimming legs are reduced to a few thin bristles, the eyes are unstalked dots, and the animal is drawn upright rather than swimming on its back.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a slender translucent segmented tube with no carapace, flip it belly-up, line eleven pairs of broad flat leaf legs along the thorax in a phase-shifted wave, put the two dark eyes on short stalks either side of the head, and warm the tail toward orange-pink.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld; all three mustReads fail at size. The body is opaque cream with a big carapace-like front ovoid against a reference that says 'no carapace at all — a bare translucent tube'; the eleven pairs of leaf-like legs are four thin straight bristles; the eyes are one unstalked dark dot rather than stalked eyes; and the upside-down swimming attitude is not depicted. Additionally it is built from the same two-lobe template as Tadpole Shrimp with only a hue change, which is its own problem.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp with an oval plate floating above it
rows.defect: The dorsal shield is a hard-edged tan oval hovering clear of the body rather than a carapace covering the front half, the two long thin appendages are drawn at the FRONT as antennae instead of the two forked filaments at the tail, and the paired dark eyes on top of the shield are absent along with the dozens of leaf legs beneath it.
rows.fix: Seat the shield onto the body so its front and side margins wrap the thorax with no gap, place two close-set dark eyes on top of it, replace the tail fan with two long thin forked caudal filaments, and pack a dense row of small leaf legs visibly protruding beneath the shield rim.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, one claim REFUTED: the tan shield is NOT floating clear of the body — it abuts the abdomen and does cover the front half, so mustRead 1 is roughly served. The rest holds: the two long thin filaments are drawn at the FRONT as antennae when they belong at the tail as forked cercopods (a genuine wrong-end error, mustRead 2 absent), the dozens of leaf legs are four bristles, and the paired dark eyes on the shield are absent so the 'helmeted' read is gone. Same template as Fairy Shrimp recolored.

rows.readsAs: a stubby six-legged soil bug
rows.defect: The furcula is drawn as a single smooth curl trailing loose behind the abdomen rather than a forked spring folded forward under the belly, so the springtail's one diagnostic mechanism reads as a tail.
rows.fix: Fork the furcula into two tines and tuck it forward along the underside of the abdomen with the tips reaching toward the mid-body, held by a small ventral catch.

rows.readsAs: beads on a string with two glass wings
rows.defect: The abdomen is a chain of separated discs with visible gaps between them and a fully detached round ball floating at the rear tip — a clear construction artifact; the huge crossed sickle mandibles of the male are reduced to two tiny pale hooks under the head.
rows.fix: Fuse the abdominal beads into one continuous soft flabby cylinder with segment lines only (no gaps, no free-floating terminal ball), and draw two long curved mandibles crossing in front of the head at roughly half the body length.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld and the artifact is unmistakable at size: the abdomen is a row of alternating light/dark spheres with visible gaps between them and a fully DETACHED ball hanging in space past the tip of the body — a construction artifact on its own. The male's huge crossed sickle mandibles are absent (only small dark hooks under the head, which read as legs). The one thing that works is the long wings folded past the abdomen, though they are glassy rather than smoky net-veined.

rows.readsAs: a wasp
rows.defect: The long downward beak-like snout is absent (only small hooks beneath the head) and the bulbous upcurled tail tip is missing, leaving a yellow-and-black banded body that reads as a wasp; the abdomen is again a chain of separated beads and the wings are clear rather than blotched black.
rows.fix: Extend a long narrow rostrum straight down from the head with the jaws at its tip, fuse the abdominal beads into a continuous tapering abdomen and curl the last two segments up over the back ending in a rounded bulb, and blotch the narrow wings with irregular black patches.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld. All three mustReads are absent: no long downward beak-like snout (just small hooks under the head), no bulbous upcurled male tail tip, and the wings are clear rather than blotched black. What is left is a yellow-and-black banded beaded abdomen that a stranger names a bee or wasp. Same beaded-abdomen template failure as Dobsonfly, slightly less severe here — the spheres overlap rather than separate and nothing is detached — so this one is a mustRead failure rather than an artifact failure.

rows.readsAs: a pink pig
rows.defect: a grey-brown bar is drawn across the muzzle from cheek to snout at a tone that matches nothing else, so it reads as a stick jammed in the mouth; the rear ends in a plain tapered stub with no curly tail
rows.fix: paint the lower jaw inside the head silhouette at snout-pink, and add the corkscrew tail from the mustReads (a 1.5-turn spiral at the rump)

rows.readsAs: a golden game-bird with a pasted ring on its side
rows.defect: the wing is a hard-outlined dark circle pasted over the flank (a ring enclosing a lighter round patch), and the comb is drawn at beak-yellow with no wattles at all
rows.fix: replace the circular wing token with a folded-wing shape that follows the body contour and shares its tone; paint comb and wattles scarlet, distinct from the bill
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed at 300px. The wing is a closed dark annulus stroke enclosing a lighter oval disc, sitting on the flank — it reads as a pasted ring, not a folded wing, and the same asset recurs on Rooster and Kestrel. Comb is drawn at beak-yellow with no wattles, so reference mustRead 'small comb and wattles' is only half met. The bird does still read as a fowl (comb, fan tail, scaly legs), so this is a FAIL on the artifact rather than on identity — the weakest FAIL in the set, but the ring is objectively there and objectively not anatomy.

rows.readsAs: a red cartoon bird with three sticks for a tail
rows.defect: the tail is three straight brown rods radiating horizontally instead of arching sickle plumes, and the same outlined-circle wing is pasted on the flank; no wattles
rows.fix: curve the tail feathers into overlapping sickles that rise then fall, and hang red wattles under the bill; drop the circular wing token
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. The tail is three straight brown rods with rounded ends radiating down-right — no arch, no curve, no sickle. Reference mustRead 'arching sickle tail plumes' absent, 'tall red comb and long wattles' half absent (red comb yes, wattles none). Same outlined-ring wing pasted on the flank, plus a pale grey halo fringe leaking around the upper back. Two of three mustReads broken.

rows.readsAs: a melon vine

rows.readsAs: an upright herb with blue star flowers

rows.readsAs: a hosta with a small red spike

rows.readsAs: a pale hosta or wild ginger with a red spike

rows.readsAs: a white agave or succulent rosette

rows.readsAs: a stiff upright herb with one blue speck on top

rows.readsAs: a cassava or castor-type shrub with hand-shaped leaves

rows.readsAs: a twining vine with small white bell flowers

rows.readsAs: a hosta or wild ginger with a white star on a wire

rows.readsAs: a clump of dead pampas grass or straw
rows.defect: The arching threads spring from ground level, so there is no tall bare three-sided stem carrying a firework burst at the very TOP — the plant's whole silhouette is inverted; the colour is dead straw-brown rather than green.
rows.fix: Raise 4-6 bare triangular green stems to about 70% of frame height with nothing on them, then explode 40+ fine drooping green threads from each apex only, and set the clump in water over a thick rhizome.
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed. The silhouette is exactly inverted: the arching threads spring from ground level, so there is no tall bare three-sided stem and no firework burst at the TOP, which is mustRead 1 and 2. Colour is dead straw-brown rather than bright green stem and rays. There are also two small detached dash-marks floating free of the plant in the upper left and upper right of the clump - a visible drawing artifact.

rows.readsAs: three small lily pads on a pond
rows.defect: Only three large discs are drawn, so the scale reads as lily pads rather than duckweed's carpet of many tiny fronds, and no disc has the single fine hair root hanging beneath it.
rows.fix: Raise the frond count to 40+ and shrink each to a few pixels so they tile the water surface, and hang one thin pale root from each disc into the dark water below.

rows.readsAs: a bare wiry bush with pink flower sprays
rows.defect: The stems carry no leaves at all, so the narrow inrolled leaves flashing white undersides are missing, and the flowers are flat upward-facing pink stars rather than drooping urn-shaped bells.
rows.fix: Clothe the twigs in narrow leaves rolled at the edge with a bright white underside showing on the turned ones, and redraw the flowers as nodding pink urns hanging from short curved pedicels.

rows.readsAs: a sundew rosette
small golden toadstools with near-black cap crowns
rows.defect: The cap is a flat convex disc with thin radial blade gills and a shading ramp that runs to near-black across the top; both defining traits — the downward-flaring funnel/vase profile and the fat blunt forking ridges — are absent, so only the yellow says chanterelle.
rows.fix: Paint the cap as a funnel flaring downward with a wavy lobed rim, replace the blade gills with thick blunt forked ridges that run down onto the stem, and clamp the cap top-shading ramp at mid-gold so the crown never darkens below the stem tone.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds at 7x. Caps are flat/slightly domed lens discs with a smooth (not wavy-lobed) margin and fine radial BLADE gill teeth at the stem junction — the reference note names this exact failure mode verbatim ("Commonly drawn with true blade gills and a flat cap; it has fat blunt forking ridges and a vase profile"). Both the funnel/vase profile and the blunt forking ridges are absent. Additionally a near-black arc bands the top of every cap and the stem is much paler than the cap, contradicting the colour row "egg-yolk golden yellow throughout, cap and stem the same colour". 2 of 3 mustReads absent plus a colour contradiction.

rows.readsAs: a pinecone on a white stalk
rows.defect: The head texture is a uniform flat diamond grid with no depth, so the pits read as a printed lattice rather than recessed chambers, and the head's lower edge overhangs the stalk like a cap skirt instead of fusing into it.
rows.fix: Draw each pit as a shadowed concavity with a lit raised ridge wall, randomise the pit grid so rows are irregular, and merge the head's bottom edge into the stalk silhouette with no overhang.

rows.readsAs: a white puffball and a striped golf ball on a shelf
rows.defect: The rind is chalk-white with white speckles instead of coal-black with pyramidal warts, the cut face is a white sphere ruled with straight parallel stripes instead of dark flesh laced with branching white veins, and the soil is a hard-edged rectangle that reads as a pasted panel.
rows.fix: Recolour the rind to near-black with raised pyramid facets, make the cut face purple-black with fine irregular branching white marbling, and feather the soil band's top and side edges instead of leaving a rectangle.
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, though the auditor's wording is partly wrong: at 3x the rind DOES carry real little pyramidal warts, not just speckles, so mustRead 1's form is met. What fails is decisive anyway — the rind is chalk-WHITE where the reference (and the species name) demand "coal-black warty rind", and the cut face inverts mustRead 2 into dark straight parallel rules on white flesh instead of a lace of white veins branching through dark flesh. The soil is also a hard-edged rectangle with abrupt vertical cut-offs, a visible drawing artifact. Defining colour absent + artifact.

rows.readsAs: gold spearhead blades stuck on a post
rows.defect: The caps are sharp-tipped golden-orange lances with no gills and no shell curve; an oyster is a grey-fawn fan or shell with white gills running down to a stubby lateral stem.
rows.fix: Swap the lance for an offset fan/shell outline with an inrolled wavy margin, recolour to pale grey-fawn, and draw white radial gills converging on a short lateral stem stub at the wood.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. Four sharp-tipped golden-orange lances on a post — same blade primitive as Bracket/Turkey Tail/Chicken/Shelf, recoloured. mustRead 2 (white gills running down to an off-centre stubby stem) is wholly absent — no gills, no stem of any kind. mustRead 3 (smooth inrolled wavy margin) is absent; the margin terminates in a point. Colour is golden-orange against a reference of "pale grey to fawn-brown cap, white gills". Only the tiers-on-wood arrangement survives.

rows.readsAs: big smooth white balls on the ground
white blades on a fence post
rows.defect: It is four thin white pointed lances — the same asset as Oyster, Turkey Tail, Chicken and Shelf recoloured — where a bracket must read as ONE thick grey-brown woody hoof jutting from the trunk with concentric growth ridges.
rows.fix: Give this species its own single half-disc hoof: a domed grey-brown top with concentric ridge bands stepping outward, a thick woody profile, and a flat cream pore underside (no gills, no multiple tiers).
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, and it is the clearest case in the set. All three mustReads are absent: no hoof or half-disc, no ridged concentric growth bands (only two hairline arcs), no pore underside. The reference row carries an explicit disambiguation — "a bracket reads as ONE thick woody hoof, the shelf as many thin tiers" — and the art is pixel-for-pixel the same four-thin-tier blade asset as Shelf Fungus with a different fill. Grey-brown zoned crust rendered as plain white.

rows.readsAs: two white pillars with flat green caps
rows.defect: No white egg sac at the base — the stalks end in a plain flat flange — and the head is a matte flat-topped green cap rather than a thimble glistening with olive-black slime.
rows.fix: Seat each stalk in a split white egg sac at ground level, and repaint the head as a bell/thimble with wet olive-black specular highlights and slime streaks running down its lower edge.

rows.readsAs: a sea urchin or spiky dark seed
rows.defect: Thin dark blue-grey needles radiate flat from a dark bluish ball; there is no leathery tan star of thick rays peeled back onto the ground, and the centre is not a pale papery sac with a pore.
rows.fix: Draw 6-8 broad triangular tan-to-grey-brown rays curling back and down to touch the ground, and set a pale grey papery spore sac with a single raised apical pore in their centre.
rows.verifyWhy: REFUTED at 8x. The auditor's description is factually wrong: the centre is NOT a dark bluish ball and the pore is NOT missing. It is a pale lilac-grey papery sphere with a distinct round dark pore on it (mustRead 2 and 3 both present), ringed by thick-based tapering wedge rays — not needles (mustRead 1 present in kind). The tile is simply under-lit, which is what collapsed it to a dark spiky ball on a 42-tile sheet. Real remaining defects are polish-grade: rays are grey-lilac rather than leathery tan, the pore sits on the front face instead of the apex, only ~6 rays, and they don't peel back onto the ground.

rows.readsAs: classic red toadstools with white spots
a green pleated parasol
rows.defect: The cap carries deep radial pleats/ribs like a Parasola, where a death cap is a smooth olive dome with only faint fibrils; and the stem base is a plain flange with no sac-like volva — the ref calls the volva the identifying feature.
rows.fix: Flatten the cap ribs into faint radiating fibril lines over a smooth olive-green surface, and add a white bag-like volva cup enclosing the bottom of the stem.

rows.readsAs: an all-white mushroom with a ringed stem
brown parasol mushrooms
rows.defect: The cap is smooth with fine radial striations instead of the cracked surface showing white flesh through the fissures, and the inrolled margin carries no white veil fringe.
rows.fix: Overlay an irregular crackle of pale cream fissures across a matt umber cap, and hang torn white veil remnants along the inrolled cap margin.

rows.readsAs: a brown button mushroom
rows.defect: The stem is a slender cylinder of even width, so the signature fat barrel bulb far thicker than the cap is missing; the white reticulation net is drawn but sits on a stem too thin to carry it, and the stem is split by a hard vertical light/dark seam down its middle.
rows.fix: Swell the stem into a barrel wider than the cap radius, tapering up into the cap, and replace the two-tone split with a single wrapped cylindrical gradient so the net reads over one surface.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of white grapes or soap bubbles
rows.defect: The body is built from overlapping smooth spheres and the spines exist only as a short fringe of about eight drips along the bottom edge; the defining full coat of long hanging icicle spines is absent.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere cluster with one rounded unbranched mass whose entire lower two-thirds is covered in long pendant spines of varying length, all hanging vertically and overlapping.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, with one correction: the spines are a band of roughly 30 strokes across the lower-middle of the mass, not "about eight drips along the bottom edge". That does not save it. At 7x the body is ~30 hard-edged spheres with individual specular highlights, with more spheres continuing BELOW the spine band, so the spines read as pasted onto the middle of a ball pile. mustRead 1 (a rounded pom-pom OF long hanging icicle spines) and mustRead 2 (spines all cascading downward) are both absent. A stranger names grapes, foam or dough.

rows.readsAs: a brown cloud or tree canopy floating over a white cone
rows.defect: The fronds are one puffy lobed brown cloud silhouette with no individual spoon-shaped caps, and the mass hovers clear of the small white stalk cone below it, so the two parts never connect.
rows.fix: Build the mass from dozens of overlapping grey-brown spoon-shaped fronds fanning out in a rosette, and root them visibly on a branched white stalk that reaches the ground.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, and it carries a genuine drawing artifact: at 3x there is a clear empty gap between the brown frond mass and the white cone on the ground — the two elements never touch, so the canopy floats. mustRead 1 (overlapping spoon-shaped fronds) is absent; it is one flat lobed cloud silhouette with thin arcs drawn on it. mustRead 2 (fronds springing from a single branched white stalk base) is absent; the base is one unbranched cone. Reads as a tree canopy.

rows.readsAs: a bouquet of long thin white mushrooms fused at the base
plain tan blades on a post
rows.defect: Each fan is a single flat ochre lance with one faint line, so the defining many-hued concentric banding (rust, ochre, blue-grey, cream, near-black) and the pale wavy cream rim are both absent; it is the shared lance asset in a different colour.
rows.fix: Make each bracket a thin semicircular fan and stripe it with 6-8 concentric bands that shift HUE as well as tone, finishing in a pale cream wavy outer rim; cluster many small fans in overlapping rosettes.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, with a correction: there are 2-3 faint concentric arcs per fan, not "one faint line". But they are all a single ochre hue, and the reference note is explicit that this is disqualifying — "The bands must vary in hue as well as tone - a single-colour ringed bracket reads as a different species." mustRead 2's pale cream wavy outer rim is absent, the shape is a pointed lance rather than a fan, and there are six blades rather than dozens of small overlapping rosettes. Same shared blade asset as Oyster/Bracket/Shelf/Chicken.

rows.readsAs: pale blue-white icicle blades
rows.defect: The shelves are painted ice-blue/white, the exact opposite of the species' defining brilliant sulphur-yellow to salmon-orange flesh with a bright yellow pore underside.
rows.fix: Recolour to a saturated salmon-orange top grading to a sulphur-yellow margin, thicken each shelf into a fleshy lobe with a suede wavy edge, and paint the underside bright yellow pores.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds without qualification. Sampled fill is RGB ~(194,210,219) — a cold ice-blue-white — against a reference whose colour line and mustReads all hinge on "brilliant sulphur-yellow to salmon-orange top, bright yellow pore underside" and "thick fleshy overlapping shelves in vivid orange with yellow margins". Colour IS the identity of this species and it is rendered at the opposite end of the wheel. Shelves are also thin pointed lances rather than thick fleshy wavy-lobed ones.

rows.readsAs: orange corn dogs on sticks in a mud patch
rows.defect: The host insect is a featureless brown oval mound with a few scratch lines — no head, legs or segmentation — and the reference is explicit that without a legible host this is just a club fungus.
rows.fix: Paint a recognisable dead insect (segmented abdomen, folded legs, head with eyes) half-buried in the litter, and have the clubs erupt from its thorax and abdominal joints rather than from a bare mound.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. The clubs themselves are good — slender stalks with swollen roughened orange fertile heads, mustReads 1 and 3 satisfied. But the host is a flat ground-level brown ellipse with a few vertical tick marks: no head, no legs, no body volume, no segmentation. It reads as a patch of soil or a shadow. The reference note is explicit and decisive: "The insect must stay legible - without a visible host it is just a club fungus."

rows.readsAs: a cluster of small glowing green mushrooms
a bare winter shrub or dead bonsai
rows.defect: Three separate bare trunks branch into hairline twigs that taper to sharp points, producing a leafless-tree silhouette; a coral fungus is one thick fused base throwing up fleshy prongs that end blunt or forked.
rows.fix: Fuse the stems into a single thick pale base, keep branch width fleshy all the way out instead of tapering to hairlines, and terminate every branch in a blunt rounded or twin-forked tip.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. Three SEPARATE trunks (mustRead 1 demands one thick fused base), branching laterally into a wide canopy rather than an upward antler cluster, with twigs that taper to hairline points instead of staying fleshy and ending blunt (mustRead 2). The silhouette is unambiguously a bare winter tree/shrub — a stranger names a plant, not a fungus. Colour (cream) and the no-caps-no-gills requirement are the only things right.

rows.readsAs: an orange fruit or peach
rows.defect: It is an opaque solid orange ball made of overlapping circles with thin dark scribbles laid on top — no translucency and no convoluted brain-like folding — and it sits on bare ground rather than bark.
rows.fix: Build the mass from broad curling gelatinous lobes with rim-lit amber thin edges so light appears to pass through, and seat it directly on a bark surface with no stem.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds, though the lobing is better than "an orange fruit" implies — at 9x there are several genuinely overlapping soft lobes. What fails: mustRead 2 (translucent enough that light passes through) is completely absent, the mass is fully opaque; mustRead 3 (sitting directly on bark) is absent, it sits on a bare tan ellipse. And the "folds" are a set of thin dark angular strokes plus one white arc laid over the lobes that cross lobe boundaries at random and read as pen scratches — a visible drawing artifact, not convolution.

rows.readsAs: crimson blades on a post
rows.defect: The brackets are bright crimson-red pointed lances (the shared lance asset again); a shelf fungus is banded ochre and umber, with flat semicircular plates stacked in tiers.
rows.fix: Recolour to ochre/umber concentric zoning, flatten each bracket into a semicircle with a flat top and a flat pale-buff underside, and step the stack outward as it descends the trunk.
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed but on narrower grounds than the auditor gave. The tiered-stack body plan is actually the one thing this tile gets right — mustRead 1 (several thin brackets in overlapping tiers) and the staircase step-out are both present, so the shared blade asset is not itself wrong HERE. What fails is colour and profile: sampled fill is RGB ~(217,66,78), a saturated crimson, against "banded ochre and umber above, pale buff pore surface below", with no banding at all; and mustRead 2 (each shelf semicircular with a flat top and flat underside) is absent — every plate ends in a sharp point. Reads as red bunting on a post.

rows.readsAs: a small white tree with a domed canopy
rows.defect: The lower half is a zone of bare smooth arching trunks rising to a dense canopy, giving a tree silhouette; the reference explicitly forbids a stem — it must be a springy cushion mat of hollow stalks forking from the ground up.
rows.fix: Begin the forking at ground level so there is no bare-trunk zone, flatten the dome into a low spreading cushion, and let the fine tips droop and nod consistently in one direction.

rows.readsAs: a green mossy stone
rows.defect: It is a solid 3-D dome with a hard silhouette edge and flat fill; the tangled white hyphal fuzz and the upright stalks each topped by a dark round spore capsule are both missing.
rows.fix: Soften the silhouette into a low spreading circular patch of white thread fuzz, and stipple the surface with hundreds of short upright stalks each carrying a dark spherical spore head.

rows.readsAs: an orange-brown rock or heap of turmeric
rows.defect: A raised orange-ochre 3-D mound — the same blob asset as Mold and Yeast, recoloured — where mildew is a chalky white-grey powder film lying flat on a surface with the substrate still visible through it.
rows.fix: Recolour to chalky white-grey and paint it as a flat semi-transparent dusting over a visible leaf or fabric substrate, with blotchy irregular patch edges instead of a domed outline.
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed, but the stated reason is partly refuted: at 3x it is NOT a deep 3-D mound — it is a flattish, semi-transparent blotchy patch with a spore dusting around the rim, so the reference's own warning about drawing it as three-dimensional fluff is largely respected. It fails on the other two counts. Sampled fill is RGB ~(83,57,24), a saturated warm brown-ochre, against "chalky white to pale grey powder"; and mustRead 3 (the surface beneath still visible through the film) cannot be met because there is no substrate at all — it floats on black. It is also the identical silhouette to Yeast with only the hue changed, so the two species are not separable.

rows.readsAs: a grey lump of dough or a stone
rows.defect: An amorphous grey mound with sparkle specks; none of the defining cell structure reads — no oval cells, no bud swelling off one side, no bud scars.
rows.fix: Replace the blob with a loose cluster of a few large translucent buff oval cells, each with a smaller round bud budding off one side and faint ring-shaped bud scars pocking the wall.
rows.verifyWhy: Holds. All three mustReads are absent: no rounded oval single cells, no bud swelling off one side, no bud scars, no loose cluster of a few cells. It is one amorphous grey polygonal mound with a sparkle field — and it is provably the same asset as Mildew (identical outline, identical speckle distribution, different fill), which means the microscopic-fungi body plan the reference note specifically asks for was never drawn.

rows.readsAs: a generic round-crowned tree with olive-yellow fruit
rows.defect: the pinnate sprays radiate straight outward like starburst spokes from a blurred green disc instead of drooping, and the loose white flower sprays are absent entirely
rows.fix: rotate each leaf spray to hang downward from a visible twig (tip below its attachment point) and add 3-5 small white panicles among the sprays

rows.readsAs: a leafy fruit tree with striped melons in the crown
rows.defect: the trunk is the same thin brown pole used by every other tree in the slice - no swollen grey barrel - and the pods sit inside a dense leafy crown instead of dangling on long cords from bare stubby branches
rows.fix: give the trunk a barrel profile (trunk width ~0.5x crown width, grey smooth), strip the crown down to a few short blunt root-like branches, and hang the velvety pods on long visible stalks below the branch line
rows.verifyWhy: 0 of 3 mustReads. Trunk is the same slim brown pole as Acacia/Wild Fig in the same slice - no swollen grey barrel, no stubby root-like top branches. The grey-brown pods sit embedded INSIDE a dense leafy crown instead of dangling on long cords, and the reference's own note says the bare 'upside-down tree' silhouette is the recognisable state. Reads as a generic fruit tree.

rows.readsAs: a generic tree with sunflowers stuck on it
rows.defect: the crown is a domed cloud blob rather than a flat-topped umbrella, and the flowers are five large yellow daisy discs with dark brown eyes; several leaf sprays float in the blur with no twig under them
rows.fix: clamp the crown to a wide flat-topped layer (height ~0.35x width, top edge horizontal), replace the daisy discs with small cream pom-pom puffballs, and add paired white thorns at the branch nodes
rows.verifyWhy: Crown is a domed cloud blob, not the flat-topped umbrella mustRead; no paired white thorns; no horizontal layering. The flowers are five large yellow ray-daisies with dark brown eyes - the reference wants puffball cream flowers and explicitly warns off even the golden pom-pom wattle read, so 'sunflowers stuck on a tree' is worse than the anti-pattern. Several feathery sprays float in the crown blur with no twig under them (visible pasted-part artifact).

rows.readsAs: a generic tree with round yellow fruit
rows.defect: bark is flat plain brown with no mottled grey flaking, and every fruit sits up in the crown - none of the signature yellow fruit littering the ground beneath

rows.readsAs: a plum tree
rows.defect: three purple stalked plums hang in the crown while the trunk is a plain slim pole - the figs are not on the wood, and there is no buttressed pale trunk or hanging aerial root
rows.fix: widen the trunk into a fused buttressed base, draw the figs as small round green-red bodies studding the trunk and lower limbs directly, and drop two or three thin aerial roots from the crown to the ground
rows.verifyWhy: 0 of 3 mustReads. Three purple stalked globes hang at twig-tip position in the crown - the reference note is explicit that 'figs sit on the wood, not at twig tips'. No buttressed pale trunk, no fused root lattice, no hanging aerial roots; the trunk is the same slim pole as Baobab and Acacia. A stranger names a plum tree.

rows.readsAs: a small fruit tree with tan berries
rows.defect: the fruit are plain tan spheres with no four-lobed papery star calyx, and the crown is a wide soft blur rather than an upright oval over dark blocky bark
rows.fix: cap each fruit with a four-pointed green calyx star, darken the trunk to near-black blocky bark, and make the crown taller than wide

rows.readsAs: one flat fan-palm leaf, or an agave
rows.defect: the blades merge into a single continuous webbed sheet with leaf veins running through it and splay sideways almost horizontally - there is no thickness, no toothed edge and no upward-curving rosette; the flower spike is a hair-thin bare wire
rows.fix: separate the blades into individual thick tapering bodies with a visible gap between them, curve them upward from a tight centre, add small teeth along each edge, and thicken the flower stalk with tubular downward-hanging orange bells rather than a bead chain
rows.verifyWhy: DOWNGRADED. The auditor's headline sub-claim is wrong at size: the flower spike is not a bare wire - it is a clearly rendered orange-red tubular spike rising well above the leaves, so mustReads 2 and 3 are both PRESENT and the harvest is correct. The blades also separate into distinct pointed triangles across the upper half; it does not read as one fan-palm leaf. What is genuinely wrong is only mustRead 1: the lower two-thirds fuses into a continuous veined sheet, the blades splay near-horizontally instead of curving upward, and there are no marginal teeth or thickness. That is a rosette-construction fix, not a lost identity - the silhouette plus the orange spike still says aloe.

rows.readsAs: a pink chrysanthemum bouquet
rows.defect: every leaf is drawn salmon-pink so the plant has no green foliage at all, and the harvest - the fat waxy crimson calyx - is absent; only magenta daisy discs appear
rows.fix: recolour the lobed leaves mid green with red veins and red stalks, and add swollen scarlet cup-shaped calyces hugging the stem at the leaf axils
rows.verifyWhy: Confirmed at size: there is no green anywhere on the plant - every leaf is drawn salmon-pink, against a reference of 'mid green with red veins'. The harvest, the fat waxy crimson calyx hugging the stem, is entirely absent; what appears instead is magenta ray-daisy discs, which is the pale hibiscus-flower error the reference note warns against, made worse. Reads as a pink chrysanthemum bouquet.

rows.readsAs: a single sprig of grey fern
rows.defect: a lone thin stem carries narrow pale mauve-grey lance leaflets that nearly vanish against the dark tile; the big paired broad crinkled toothed green leaves and the one-sided seed-capsule spikes are both missing
rows.fix: replace the leaflets with large opposite broad ovals (toothed, crinkled, mid green with purple backs) on a square stem, and add a slim one-sided spike of tiny seed capsules at the top
rows.verifyWhy: One thin stem carrying narrow pale mauve-grey lance leaflets in a pinnate ladder. The reference wants LARGE PAIRED broad oval coarsely toothed crinkled leaves on square stems, mid green - the drawn leaflets are narrow, untoothed, not broad, and grey rather than green. The one-sided seed-capsule spikes (mustRead 3) are absent. Nothing survives; reads as a fern sprig and nearly vanishes against the dark tile.

rows.readsAs: a clump of dry ornamental pampas grass
rows.defect: the blades are straw-yellow and thin with no stout jointed cane behind them, and the grain head is a narrow rust-coloured ribbed stick capped by a triangular funnel that reads as a screw or nail
rows.fix: add a thick upright jointed green cane the blades alternate from, colour the blades mid green with a white midrib, and replace the head with a heavy compact red-brown panicle wider than the cane
rows.verifyWhy: 0 of 3 mustReads. Blades emerge straight from a basal clump with no stout jointed cane behind them, they are thin and straw-yellow with no white midrib, and the 'heavy compact seed head' is a narrow rust ribbed cylinder on a bare wire capped by a triangular funnel that reads as a screw or nail. The grain-crop identity is entirely gone - a stranger says ornamental pampas grass.

rows.readsAs: a pink feathery ornamental herb
rows.defect: the huge palmate star leaves are drawn as dozens of tiny salmon-pink pinwheels, so the plant's whole identity is gone; there is no red spiny capsule spike and no hollow red stem
rows.fix: make the leaves few and very large (each roughly a third of the plant's height), deep green to bronze-red with 7-11 pointed lobes on long stalks, and add one upright cluster of bristly red capsules above them
rows.verifyWhy: The huge palmate star leaf - the entire identity - is rendered as ~20 tiny salmon-pink pinwheels that read as flowers, not foliage, at every size. rows.readsAs: a pink echinacea

rows.readsAs: an ox-eye daisy or chamomile
rows.defect: a sparse open V of a few bare stems replaces the dense twiggy rounded bush; leaves are plain untoothed ovals and the flowers are many-rayed white daisies with a brown eye
rows.fix: fill the silhouette into a dense rounded twiggy mass, serrate the glossy leaf edges, and redraw the flowers as 5-6 broad rounded white petals around a fat golden stamen boss, nodding

The flowers are many-rayed white daisies with a brown eye rather than nodding camellia flowers with a yellow stamen boss, and the harvest (bud plus two pale top leaves) is nowhere. rows.readsAs: a small tree with tiny red berry clumps

rows.readsAs: a sago palm or cycad
rows.defect: the crown is once-pinnate palm fronds rather than long-stalked deeply lobed palmate leaves, the green trunk forks into a truncated dead-end stub that supports nothing, and there is one striped melon at the fork instead of fruit clustered on the stem

rows.verifyWhy: Two independent FAIL triggers. (1) The crown is once-pinnate palm/cycad fronds - visibly the SAME frond asset as Tree Fern Shoots in this slice - where the reference demands long-stalked deeply lobed palmate leaves, and the trunk is thick and forked rather than a slim scarred stem with a small tuft. rows.readsAs: a small upright blue-berried bush - indistinguishable from the Blueberry tile
